summary: Audit and rewrite all 261 Qpio discovery hooks against the curiosity-pull spec, then adversarially verify each rewrite
logs: 261 hooks returned · 219 rewritten · 48 truth flags · 15 spoiler flags

hooks.en: Everyone knows it was built to survive a nuclear attack. The head of ARPA said otherwise.
hooks.fr: Tout le monde sait qu'il devait survivre à une guerre nucléaire. Le patron de l'ARPA a démenti.
hooks.note: Verified on WP/ARPANET: Charles Herzfeld, ARPA Director 1965-67, "The ARPANET was not started to create a Command and Control System that would survive a nuclear attack, as many now claim." Quiz answer (Stanford Research Institute) untouched. FR 95 chars, under cap.

hooks.en: There is a town in Iowa named after him. He never set foot in America.
hooks.fr: Une petite ville de l'Iowa porte son nom. Il n'a jamais mis les pieds en Amérique.
hooks.note: WP/Elkader, Iowa: "The city is named after a Muslim Algerian leader, the Emir Abdelkader." Pop. 1,209 — legally a city, but 'town'/'petite ville' is fair for that size. His documented life runs Algeria - France (imprisonment) - Bursa - Damascus - Mecca; no American travel. All four checks pass.

hooks.en: Large stretches of the land their ancestors lived on are now under the sea.
hooks.fr: De vastes portions du pays de leurs ancêtres se trouvent aujourd'hui sous la mer.
hooks.note: WP/Aboriginal Australians, near-verbatim: "Aboriginal people once lived across large areas of the continental shelf that were later inundated by postglacial sea-level rise." Pull is the mildest in this slice (a reader who knows about ice ages can half-close it) but it is not generic and does not answer itself. Passes.

hooks.en: Negative temperatures exist in the lab. They are hotter than every positive one.
hooks.fr: Des températures négatives existent en laboratoire. Elles sont plus chaudes que les positives.
hooks.note: EN is true and strong — WP/Negative temperature: "a system with a truly negative temperature on the Kelvin scale is hotter than any system with a positive temperature", achieved by Purcell & Pound 1951 and Braun et al. 2013. FR FAILED: it dropped "in the lab", so the French sentence reads as a claim about -10 °C and is then simply false. Restored the qualifier. (pulls flag set false only because the FR as shipped would have read as nonsense, not as a gap; EN pull is fine.)

hooks.en: Her mother steered her into mathematics partly to stop her turning out like her father.
hooks.fr: Sa mère l'a orientée vers les maths en partie pour qu'elle ne ressemble pas à son père.
hooks.note: WP/Ada Lovelace verbatim: "Her mother's obsession with rooting out any of the insanity of which she accused Byron was one of the reasons that Ada was taught mathematics from an early age." "partly" correctly hedges "one of the reasons". No spoiler (quiz answer is the topic name). Passes.

hooks.en: Two elephants can hold a conversation across open country, at a pitch you cannot hear.
hooks.fr: Deux éléphants se parlent à des kilomètres, sur des fréquences que nous n'entendons pas.
hooks.note: EN supported by WP/African bush elephant: "Rumbles ... cover a broad range of frequencies which are mostly below what a human can hear" and "Infrasonic rumbles can travel vast distances." FR FAILED on idiom: "se parler ... SUR des sons" is not French (one speaks sur des fréquences, not sur des sons). Rewritten; 87 chars.

hooks.en: One word at the heart of computing is his own name, mangled by Latin.
hooks.fr: Un mot au cœur de l'informatique n'est que son nom, déformé par le latin.
hooks.note: OVERSTATED: "every time you talk about computers" is false — you do not say 'algorithm' in every sentence about computers. Same defect in FR ("revient chaque fois que"). Underlying fact is solid: 'algorithm'/'algorism' derive from Algoritmi/Algorismi, the Latinised forms of his name. Rewritten to claim only what is true, and the gap (which word?) is preserved.

hooks.en: Russia sold Alaska because it expected to lose it in a war — to somebody else.
hooks.fr: La Russie a vendu l'Alaska de peur de le perdre dans une guerre — face à un tout autre pays.
hooks.note: WP/Alaska Purchase confirms the motive: "the hard-to-defend colony would be easily conquered by British forces based in neighboring Canada in any future conflict", hence the sale to the US. FR FAILED on grammar: Alaska is MASCULINE in French (l'Alaska, en Alaska), so "de peur de LA perdre" is wrong — corrected to "le perdre".

hooks.en: One form of carbon is named after an architect, because it looks like his buildings.
hooks.fr: Une forme du carbone porte le nom d'un architecte, tant elle ressemble à ses bâtiments.
hooks.note: True: buckminsterfullerene is named for Buckminster Fuller (WP describes him as "American architect, systems theorist, writer, designer, inventor") because it resembles his geodesic domes. FR FAILED on spacing: the colon needs an espace insécable and the source has a plain space (I found ZERO U+00A0 in the whole 2,090-line hook bank, and this channel cannot emit the character). Fixed structurally instead — comma replaces the colon, so no no-break space is required.

hooks.en: In its entire length, not one bridge crosses the Amazon's main channel.
hooks.fr: Sur toute sa longueur, aucun pont ne franchit le cours principal de l'Amazone.
hooks.note: Strong negative claim, so I checked it hard: still true as of 2026. The Manaus-Iranduba bridge crosses the Rio Negro and the Nanay bridge (Iquitos) crosses the Nanay — both tributaries. The Solimões crossing at Manacapuru remains a plan only. Passes.

hooks.en: Between record flights, she was selling her own line of clothing in Macy's. Why?
hooks.fr: Entre deux vols record, elle vendait sa propre ligne de vêtements chez Macy's. Pourquoi ?
hooks.note: Fact holds — WP/Amelia Earhart: her "active living" clothing lines "were sold in stores such as Macy's", and it does sit between the 1932 Atlantic solo and the 1935 Honolulu-Oakland solo. FR content and idiom are fine; fr_ok is false ONLY on the space before "?", which must be U+00A0. I cannot emit that character in this channel, so the string returned is unchanged — apply mechanically at merge (regex over the whole bank, not a rewrite: no hook currently has one).

hooks.en: Only one event is recorded from the first thirteen Games. Everything else came later.
hooks.fr: Une seule épreuve est attestée aux treize premiers Jeux. Tout le reste est venu après.
hooks.note: WP/Ancient Olympic Games verbatim: "The only event recorded at the first thirteen games was the stade, a straight-line sprint of just over 192 metres." "recorded"/"attestée" matches the source exactly — no overstatement. Quiz answer (Greece) not touched. Passes.

hooks.en: The point on Earth farthest from its centre is not Everest. It is in the Andes.
hooks.fr: Le point le plus éloigné du centre de la Terre n'est pas l'Everest. Il est dans les Andes.
hooks.note: Chimborazo (Ecuadorian Andes) is the point on Earth's surface farthest from the geocentre — standard, undisputed. Naming "the Andes" is not a spoiler: it is the card title the reader is already looking at, and the quiz ("longest mountain range") is already answered. Passes.

hooks.en: The Pemón have their own name for it. A visiting pilot's surname is the one that stuck.
hooks.fr: Les Pemón ont leur propre nom pour elle. C'est celui d'un pilote étranger qui s'est imposé.
hooks.note: True: Kerepakupai Merú in Pemón; named in English for aviator Jimmie Angel, who landed on the tepui in 1937. Does not name Venezuela, so the quiz answer is safe. Best decolonial framing in the slice — names the people first, the outsider second, and no "discovered". Passes.

hooks.en: Most temples at Angkor face east. This one faces west, and scholars still argue why.
hooks.fr: La plupart des temples d'Angkor regardent vers l'est. Celui-ci regarde l'ouest. Pourquoi ?
hooks.note: TWO failures. (1) Spoiler: the hook says "Khmer temple" and the quiz answer is "Khmer Empire" — the card title (Angkor Wat) does not contain it, so the hook hands over the answer. (2) Overstated: WP says "Unlike MOST Khmer temples", and Freeman & Jacques "note that several other temples of Angkor depart from the typical eastern orientation" — so "nearly every" is too strong. Rewritten to "Most temples at Angkor". The "scholars still argue why" clause is accurate (Glaize/Coedès funerary theory vs the Vishnu-west theory). FR also carries the U+00A0-before-"?" issue — fix at merge.

hooks.en: Long before the ice, Antarctica had forests. They are still there — as coal.
hooks.fr: L'Antarctique fut longtemps couvert de forêts. Elles y sont toujours, sous forme de charbon.
hooks.note: The coal claim is solid — WP/Antarctica: Permian glossopterids "grew in waterlogged soils, which formed extensive coal deposits", and "low-grade coal is known to exist across many parts of the Transantarctic Mountains". But "forested for much of its history" OVERSTATES: forests span roughly the Permian to the Eocene, a slice of a continent billions of years old. Replaced with "Long before the ice", which is unimpeachable and keeps the pull. FR passes as written ("longtemps" is the safe form) — left unchanged.

hooks.en: A speech was written for the president in case the two men could not leave the Moon.
hooks.fr: Un discours présidentiel était prêt au cas où les deux hommes ne pourraient pas repartir.
hooks.note: William Safire's "In Event of Moon Disaster" memo for Nixon, 18 July 1969 — documented and undisputed. Names neither astronaut, so the quiz answer (Neil Armstrong) is safe. FR is idiomatic and 88 chars. Passes.

hooks.en: It does not fly south in a straight line. The detour is deliberate.
hooks.fr: Il ne descend pas vers le sud en ligne droite. Le détour est volontaire.
hooks.note: WP/Arctic tern: "The birds follow a somewhat convoluted course in order to take advantage of prevailing winds" — the 2010 tracking study showed earlier straight-line assumptions underestimated the distance. "Deliberate"/"volontaire" is a shade anthropomorphic for evolved behaviour but is not a factual overstatement. Short, and it withholds the payoff. Passes.

hooks.en: An emperor won a war, then spent his reign apologising for it in stone.
hooks.fr: Un empereur gagne une guerre, puis passe son règne à s'en excuser dans la pierre.

hooks.en: One of the driest places on Earth turns into a field of flowers. Where do they come from?
hooks.fr: L'un des lieux les plus secs de la planète se couvre parfois de fleurs. D'où sortent-elles ?
hooks.note: Desierto florido is real — WP/Atacama: "Rare rainfall events cause the flowering desert phenomenon in the southern Atacama Desert", September to November in years with sufficient rain. The hedges "One of the driest" and FR "parfois" keep it honest (it is the southern margin, not the hyperarid core). fr_ok false ONLY for the U+00A0 before "?" — mechanical merge-time fix, string returned unchanged.

hooks.en: A large share of Athenian officials were never elected. They were chosen by lottery.
hooks.fr: Une grande part des magistrats athéniens n'étaient pas élus. Ils étaient tirés au sort.
hooks.note: Sortition filled the great majority of Athenian magistracies; only a handful of posts (generals, some financial officers) were elected. "A large share" / "une grande part" is deliberately unquantified, so no number to get wrong. FR agreement ("une grande part des magistrats ... n'étaient pas") is accepted usage. Passes.

hooks.en: Every proton in a nucleus repels every other. Something stronger holds them together.
hooks.fr: Dans un noyau, chaque proton repousse les autres. Quelque chose de plus fort les retient.
hooks.note: Electrostatic repulsion between every proton pair, overcome by the residual strong force — correct, and the hook deliberately withholds the name of that force. It builds on the just-answered fact rather than restating it, and the quiz answer ("in the nucleus") is the card title anyway. Passes.

hooks.en: He insisted the Republic had been restored and that he was merely its first citizen.
hooks.fr: Il assurait que la République était rétablie et qu'il n'était que le premier des citoyens.
hooks.note: "He was just a citizen" is wrong. The Senate's title was princeps — "FIRST citizen" (WP/Augustus) — and he held the consulship, then tribunician power and imperium; he never claimed to be a private citizen. The verified claim is the façade: "he would restore the façade of a free republic". Rewritten to that, which also removes the restatement of the quiz stem ("Rome's first emperor" repeated the question back at the reader).

hooks.en: A bat can weigh less than a mouse and still live past forty years.
hooks.fr: Une chauve-souris peut peser moins qu'une souris et vivre plus de quarante ans.
hooks.note: Both halves are the same animal: Brandt's bat (Myotis brandtii) weighs 5-7 g against a house mouse's 12-30 g, and the Siberian record individual was banded in 1964 and recovered at 41+ years (Guinness: longest-lived bat). "past forty" is exact, not rounded up. The souris/chauve-souris pairing makes the French land harder than the English. Passes.

hooks.en: One treaty clause said 'may' in Amharic and 'must' in the other version. A war followed.
hooks.fr: Le traité n'avait pas le même sens en amharique et dans l'autre version. La guerre a suivi.
hooks.note: SPOILER: "in Italian" hands over the quiz answer (Italy), which the card title does not contain. Fact itself checks out — WP/Treaty of Wuchale: Article XVII used a verb forming "a permissive clause in Amharic and a mandatory one in Italian", Menelik II denounced the treaty in 1894, Italy invaded in 1895. Rewrite keeps the whole gap and is better on the decolonial rubric: Amharic is named, the coloniser's text is "the other version".

hooks.en: The army beaten here was a fraction of the invading force. The rest had already left.
hooks.fr: L'armée battue ici n'était qu'un détachement. Le gros des troupes était déjà reparti.
hooks.note: SPOILER: the hook opened with "The Mongols", the verbatim quiz answer, which the card title does not give away. Fact verified — WP/Ain Jalut: Hulegu "returned to Mongolia with the bulk of his army ... leaving approximately 10,000 troops west of the Euphrates under the command of Kitbuqa". Deliberately state no reason for the withdrawal: WP now attributes it to logistics and summer pasture (Hulegu's own words, 1980s documents), NOT the death of Möngke as older accounts had it — a hook asserting the old reason would have been a defect.

hooks.en: Europeans saw these castings and decided Africans could not have made them.
hooks.fr: Devant ces bronzes, les Européens ont conclu que des Africains n'avaient pas pu les faire.

hooks.en: Binary was written down in India over two thousand years ago. The subject was poetry.
hooks.fr: Le binaire a été décrit en Inde il y a plus de deux mille ans, à propos de poésie.
hooks.note: ROUNDED THE WRONG WAY: WP/Binary number dates Pingala to "c. 2nd century BC", i.e. about 2,200 years — "two thousand years ago" states a round number as fact and understates it. "over two thousand" is true on every proposed dating of Pingala. Content is right: he "developed a binary system for describing prosody" in the Chandaḥśāstra (laghu/guru syllables), so "the subject was poetry" holds. FR recast without the colon so no espace insécable is needed.

hooks.en: The survivors came out of it better paid. That was not a coincidence.
hooks.fr: Les survivants en sont sortis mieux payés. Ce n'était pas un hasard.

hooks.en: A calf of this species puts on about ninety kilos a day. On milk alone.
hooks.fr: Le petit de cette espèce prend quelque quatre-vingt-dix kilos par jour. Uniquement au lait.

hooks.en: Lower the pressure far enough and water will boil and freeze at the same moment.
hooks.fr: Baissez assez la pression : l'eau se met à bouillir et à geler en même temps.
hooks.note: Triple point (611.657 Pa, 273.16 K): all three phases coexist; WP's own image caption is 'Water boiling at 0 °C using a vacuum pump'. Quiz answer is 100 °C at sea level - not touched. Unchanged; fr emitted with U+00A0 before the colon (source file has zero nbsp).

hooks.en: Why does a country with no coastline still maintain a navy?
hooks.fr: Pourquoi un pays sans littoral entretient-il encore une marine de guerre ?

hooks.en: The first person to write down rules for zero got one of them wrong.
hooks.fr: Le premier à écrire les règles du zéro s'est trompé sur l'une d'elles.

hooks.en: A constitution reserved land for this capital in 1891. Nobody broke ground for 65 years.
hooks.fr: Une constitution réserve le terrain de cette capitale en 1891. Les travaux attendront 65 ans.
hooks.note: FAIL (both languages carry it). No law 'created this capital' in 1891: the 1891 Constitution only reserved 14,400 km2 in the central plateau for a future federal capital; Brasília itself was created by Law 2.874 of 1956. Arithmetic (1891 to 1956 = 65 years) is right. Rewritten to say what the 1891 text actually did.

hooks.en: A tree cut down in 1964 turned out to be nearly 5,000 years old. Nobody knew beforehand.
hooks.fr: Un arbre abattu en 1964 s'est révélé vieux de près de 5 000 ans. Personne ne s'en doutait.
hooks.note: FAIL on the superlative, in both languages. WP calls Prometheus 'the oldest known non-clonal organism AT THE TIME'; Methuselah was later redated to 4,850, and Harlan's 2010 measurement of a living 5,062-year bristlecone (tree never relocated after his death in 2013) makes 'oldest ever recorded' contestable. The verified core - felled 1964, at least 4,862 and possibly over 5,000 years, 'those involved did not know of its world-record age before the cutting' - survives without the superlative.

hooks.en: Why does a brand-new 1 TB drive show up on your computer as 931 GB?
hooks.fr: Pourquoi un disque neuf de 1 To s'affiche-t-il en 931 Go sur votre ordinateur ?
hooks.note: Verified: WP 'Binary prefix' carries this exact example - 'a hard drive marketed as 1 TB could be reported as having only 931 GB' (10^12 / 2^30 = 931.32). Quiz answer (8 bits) is a different fact entirely. Strongest hook in the slice. Unchanged; nbsp added in '1 To', '931 Go' and before '?'.

hooks.en: A city of thousands emptied out by 1350. Nobody has settled on why.
hooks.fr: Des milliers d'habitants, puis plus personne vers 1350. On ignore toujours pourquoi.
hooks.note: EN passes: WP gives peak 6,000-40,000, 'by 1350 CE the city was abandoned', and lists competing environmental/social/political theories with no single agreed cause. Quiz answer (St. Louis) correctly withheld - the previous version's 'Illinois' would have been near-redundant. FR reworked: 'une ville de milliers d'habitants' is off (French wants 'plusieurs milliers'); new line is idiomatic and punchier.

hooks.en: This capital may be named after a planet that happened to be rising.
hooks.fr: Cette capitale doit peut-être son nom à une planète qui se levait ce jour-là.

hooks.en: Why was this song recorded in a Paris studio and not the band's usual London one?
hooks.fr: Pourquoi ce titre a-t-il été enregistré à Paris, et non dans le studio londonien habituel ?
hooks.note: SPOILER. The quiz answer is literally 'Liverpool' and the hook (both languages) hands it back. Paris fact itself is sound (EMI Pathé Marconi, 29 Jan 1964). I did NOT use WP's 'only English-language track recorded outside the UK' line as the new angle: the 1961 Hamburg Polydor sessions ('Ain't She Sweet') are a plausible counterexample, so that absolute is not safe to ship. Rewritten around the Paris-vs-Abbey-Road contrast, which is unimpeachable.

hooks.en: A library here keeps its front door in one country and its books in the other.
hooks.fr: Sur cette frontière, une bibliothèque a son entrée dans un pays et ses livres dans l'autre.
hooks.note: Verified on the Haskell Free Library and Opera House: 'The library collection and the theater stage are located in Stanstead, Quebec, but the main entrance and most theater seats are located in Derby Line, Vermont.' Neither country named, so no redundancy with the quiz answer. Unchanged.

hooks.en: Architects across the British Empire boycotted the contest to design this capital. Why?
hooks.fr: Les architectes britanniques ont boycotté le concours pour dessiner cette capitale. Pourquoi ?
hooks.note: 'Across the British Empire' checks out verbatim: WP says the 1911-12 competition 'was boycotted by the Royal Institute of British Architects, the Institution of Civil Engineers and their affiliated bodies throughout the British Empire' - over King O'Malley insisting on judging it himself. (Engineers boycotted too, so the hook understates rather than overstates.) Unchanged; nbsp before '?'.

hooks.en: Legend says a queen took only the land one oxhide could cover — and got a hill.
hooks.fr: Une peau de bœuf, disent les récits, suffit à une reine pour fonder une ville.

hooks.en: Tchaikovsky hid this instrument from rival composers until opening night. Then everyone heard it.
hooks.fr: Tchaïkovski a caché cet instrument à ses rivaux jusqu'à la première. Puis on l'a entendu.

hooks.en: A chip hit 3 GHz in 2002. Clock speeds have crawled ever since. What stopped them?
hooks.fr: Un processeur atteignait 3 GHz en 2002. Vingt ans plus tard, à peine le double. Pourquoi ?
hooks.note: EN holds: Pentium 4 3.06 GHz shipped November 2002; NetBurst topped out at 3.8 GHz and today's ceiling is ~6 GHz, so 'crawled' is fair for a ~2x gain in 24 years. FR failed: 'la fréquence stagne' asserts no progress, which is false - it roughly doubled. New FR states the doubling and keeps the pull. nbsp in '3 GHz' and before '?'.

hooks.en: A weighted rope sounded this place in 1875 — and missed the true bottom by over 2 km.
hooks.fr: Une corde lestée a sondé ce gouffre en 1875 : elle a manqué le vrai fond de plus de 2 km.
hooks.note: FAIL, both languages. 1875 did not find 'the deepest place on Earth': HMS Challenger recorded 4,475 fathoms (8,184 m) at station 225 on 23 March 1875, within about fifteen miles of the deepest spot; the true maximum (10,935 +/- 6 m) was not established until Challenger II in 1951 and later surveys. 'By accident' is fine ('baffling winds' pushed her off course) and 'weighted rope' is right (Baillie-weighted marked rope) - the discovery claim is what overstates. Rewrite keeps rope + date and makes the 2,751 m shortfall the hook.

hooks.en: This cat cannot roar. Hear it once and you will look up, expecting a bird.
hooks.fr: Ce félin ne rugit pas. Entendez-le une fois : vous chercherez l'oiseau des yeux.
hooks.note: FAIL on pull: it answers itself. 'It chirps, and it sounds like a bird' delivers the mechanism AND the comparison in the same breath, leaving nothing to tap for; the opening also restates the quiz question ('fastest land animal'). Facts are sound - roaring is limited to the four Panthera species, and WP describes the cheetah chirp as 'an intense bird-like call' - so I kept the tension and withheld the payoff. FR was fine in itself; replaced only to track the new EN.

hooks.en: The "floating gardens" never floated. So what has been holding them up?
hooks.fr: Les « jardins flottants » n'ont jamais flotté. Qu'est-ce qui les tient en place ?
hooks.note: SPOILER, both languages: the quiz answer is 'Mexico City' / 'Mexico' and the hook opens with it. The claim is otherwise correct - WP: chinampas are 'artificial islands ... created by interweaving reeds with stakes beneath the lake's surface', anchored with āhuexōtl willow and āhuēhuētl cypress at the corners. Dropping the city name loses nothing and sharpens the gap.

hooks.en: A town the desert is burying still keeps manuscripts older than the printing press.
hooks.fr: Une ville que le sable enterre conserve des manuscrits plus vieux que l'imprimerie.

hooks.en: The yellow in an autumn leaf was already there all summer, hidden.
hooks.fr: Le jaune des feuilles d'automne était déjà là tout l'été, simplement caché.

hooks.en: Spain arrested him in 1500 and shipped him home a prisoner. What had he done out there?
hooks.fr: En 1500, l'Espagne l'arrête aux Caraïbes et le renvoie prisonnier. Qu'avait-il fait là-bas ?
hooks.note: Verified: Bobadilla had Columbus jailed in Santo Domingo in September 1500 and sent to Spain in custody in early October, on accusations including bribe-taking, enslaving the Indigenous population and treason. Quiz answer (Atlantic) untouched. Decolonial rubric met - the hook points at the governorship record rather than the 'discovery' myth, and 'What had he done out there?' invites exactly that. Unchanged.

hooks.en: Science got this basic number about our own bodies wrong for thirty years.
hooks.fr: Pendant trente ans, la science s'est trompée sur un chiffre de notre corps.

hooks.en: She lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.
hooks.fr: Elle a vécu plus près du premier pas sur la Lune que de la construction des pyramides de Gizeh.
hooks.note: EN is exact (Great Pyramid c. 2560 BCE, Cleopatra d. 30 BCE = ~2,530 years; 30 BCE to 1969 = ~1,999 years). FR failed on precision, not style: generic 'des pyramides' includes Middle Kingdom and Kushite pyramids built long after Giza, which makes the comparison false. Pinned to Gizeh (95 chars).

hooks.en: How did a Babylonian king's law stone end up buried in what is now Iran?
hooks.fr: Comment la stèle des lois d'un roi de Babylone a-t-elle fini enterrée en Iran ?
hooks.note: Verified: stele excavated from the Susa acropolis tell (modern Iran) Dec 1901-Jan 1902, carried there as Elamite plunder (Scheil: Shutruk-Nakhunte; Roth: taken from Sippar). 'Buried' is fair for a tell excavation. Hammurabi is not named, so the quiz answer survives. Unchanged; nbsp before '?'.

hooks.en: Ostriches never bury their heads in sand. Something they really do started the myth.
hooks.fr: L'autruche ne se cache jamais la tête dans le sable. Un vrai comportement a lancé la légende.
hooks.note: Myth is false and the 'real behaviour' clause is supported - ostriches turn eggs in shallow sand nests several times a day and press head and neck flat to the ground when threatened, both of which read as burying from a distance (WP 'Head in the sand' misconception; that section body would not render for me, so I cross-checked WP List of common misconceptions and Live Science). Naming the bird is not a spoiler here: it is the card's topic name, already on screen. Unchanged.

hooks.en: Why did the man who invented the mouse never receive a cent in royalties?
hooks.fr: Pourquoi l'inventeur de la souris n'a-t-il jamais touché la moindre redevance ?
hooks.note: FAIL on precision. The checkable claim is narrower than 'never earn a cent': WP says Engelbart 'never received any royalties for the invention of the mouse' - SRI held the patent and licensed it to Apple for 'something like $40,000', while he drew an SRI salary throughout and later took the Lemelson-MIT prize. Tightened to royalties, which is bulletproof and loses no pull. FR also had a clumsy 'touché un centime dessus'; now uses 'redevance', the correct term for a patent royalty.

hooks.en: One customer's furious complaint about bad copper survives, in clay, from 1750 BCE.
hooks.fr: Un client furieux s'est plaint de son cuivre. Sa lettre d'argile date de 1750 av. J.-C.
hooks.note: EN verified: the complaint tablet to Ea-nāṣir, c. 1750 BC, from Nanni over sub-grade copper ingots; Guinness lists it as the oldest written customer complaint. Sumerians not named, so no spoiler (the tablet is Old Babylonian, and the hook wisely does not attribute it). FR failed on grammar - 'nous est parvenue de 1750 av. J.-C.' is not French; rewritten around 'lettre d'argile', which also restores the 'in clay' detail the FR had dropped.

hooks.en: Some call it the world's first human rights charter. Most historians do not.
hooks.fr: Beaucoup y voient la première charte des droits humains. Les historiens, beaucoup moins.
hooks.note: 'Most historians do not' is if anything conservative: WP records the Shah's 'first charter of human rights' framing and scholars rejecting it as anachronistic, tendentious propaganda over what is a conventional Mesopotamian building inscription. Cyrus is not named in the hook. Good decolonial fit - two perspectives, neither flattened. Unchanged.

hooks.en: Barely 2% of your DNA codes for proteins. Biologists still argue over the other 98%.
hooks.fr: À peine 2 % de votre ADN code pour des protéines. Les biologistes débattent encore du reste.
hooks.note: EN verified: WP Human genome gives coding DNA at 'about 1-2% of the genome' and states there is 'no consensus in the literature on the amount of functional DNA', estimates running from 10% to 80% functional - so both halves of the hook hold. Quiz answer (nucleus) untouched. FR failed: French genetics says 'coder pour', not 'coder des', and '2 %' needs the espace insécable.

hooks.en: Why does part of this river vanish underground and come back up in the wrong sea?
hooks.fr: Pourquoi une partie de ce fleuve s'enfonce-t-elle sous terre pour ressortir dans une autre mer ?
hooks.note: Verified: Danube Sinkhole article — river sinks between Immendingen/Fridingen (~155 days/yr), resurfaces at the Aachtopf, reaches the North Sea via Lake Constance and the Rhine, not the Black Sea. 'Come back up in the wrong sea' is a compression (it resurfaces in a spring that drains to the wrong sea) but the claim survives. Quiz answer (Four capitals) untouched. 81/96 chars.

hooks.en: What did Egyptian embalmers want from this lake? Surely not the salt.
hooks.fr: Que venaient chercher les embaumeurs égyptiens dans ce lac ? Sûrement pas le sel.
hooks.note: Verified verbatim: 'Egyptian mummification processes used asphalt imported from the Dead Sea region'; article calls it a lake throughout. Answer (Dead Sea) not named — 'this lake' used. Strong gap: the reader cannot guess bitumen. 68/80 chars.

hooks.en: In 1772 a chemist burned a diamond with sunlight. Nothing was left but gas.
hooks.fr: En 1772, un chimiste a brûlé un diamant au soleil. Il n'en est resté qu'un gaz.
hooks.note: Verified verbatim in Diamond: Lavoisier, 1772, lens focusing sun on a diamond in oxygen, 'the only product of the combustion was carbon dioxide'. Naming diamond is not a spoiler — it is the card's own topic name, and the quiz tested Mohs hardness. 74/78 chars.

hooks.en: One of these islands still has its Iñupiat village. The Soviet state emptied the other.
hooks.fr: L'une de ces îles a toujours son village iñupiat. L'État soviétique a vidé l'autre.
hooks.note: FAILED truthful. 'Both islands were Inupiat home ground until 1948' wrongly implies Little Diomede also ceased — it is still an Iñupiat village today ('unlike Alaska's neighboring Little Diomede Island, it has no permanent native population'). Also the article dates the base to 1948 and the relocation to after it, not the emptying to 1948. Rewrite keeps the verified core (Big Diomede 'originally inhabited by Iñupiat'; 'the Soviet government relocated the indigenous population'), names the actor instead of using an agentless passive (decolonial rubric), and uses the local spelling. 87/83 chars.

hooks.en: Nine Nobel nominations, no prize. In 1906 the academy voted him down by one vote.
hooks.fr: Neuf nominations au Nobel, aucun prix : en 1906, l'Académie l'a écarté à une voix près.
hooks.note: Both numbers check out: nine nominations (3 in 1905, 4 in 1906, 2 in 1907) and 'the majority of the academy chose Moissan by a margin of one vote'. Quiz answer is his own name, shown as the topic anyway; the gap (who blocked him, and why) is Arrhenius and is not given away. 80/86 chars.

hooks.en: Almost every Maya book was burned. Three or four survived. This is one.
hooks.fr: Presque tous les livres mayas ont brûlé. Trois ou quatre restent. Voici l'un d'eux.

hooks.en: Planes once dropped it into clouds to make rain. Something else does that job now.
hooks.fr: Des avions en ont lâché dans les nuages pour faire pleuvoir. Aujourd'hui, on fait autrement.
hooks.note: FAILED pulls. The mosquito claim is true ('Dry ice can be used as bait to trap mosquitoes, bedbugs... due to their attraction to carbon dioxide') but the hook answers itself: the reader has just been told dry ice is frozen CO2, and everyone knows breath is CO2, so the gap closes in one beat. Replaced with the cloud-seeding fact from the same article ('altering cloud precipitation... widely used in experiments in the US in the 1950s and early 1960s before it was replaced by silver iodide') — two gaps, neither closable from 'it's frozen CO2'. 81/91 chars.

hooks.en: It was built to compute artillery tables. Its first real job was the hydrogen bomb.
hooks.fr: Conçu pour calculer des tables de tir, il a d'abord servi à la bombe H.
hooks.note: FAILED fr_ok — dangling participle: 'Conçu pour des tables de tir, sa toute première tâche...' attaches 'conçu' to 'tâche', a participe mal rattaché in French. EN verified and unchanged: 'designed... to calculate artillery firing tables' / 'its first program was a study of the feasibility of the thermonuclear weapon' (December 1945). Fixed FR restores the machine as subject. 82/70 chars.

hooks.en: Why do some minutes have 61 seconds in them?
hooks.fr: Pourquoi certaines minutes durent-elles 61 secondes ?
hooks.note: True: a leap second is inserted as 23:59:60, giving a 61-second minute; the article covers UTC leap-second adjustment and the slowing rotation. Nothing of the quiz answer (Earth spinning on its axis) is given. Shortest and one of the strongest hooks in the slice. 44/53 chars.

hooks.en: A private apartment sits at the very top. Eiffel kept it for himself and hosted Edison.
hooks.fr: Tout en haut se cache un appartement privé : celui d'Eiffel, où il recevait Edison.
hooks.note: Verified: 'a small apartment reserved for Gustave Eiffel to entertain guests' on the third (top) level, and 'Eiffel invited Edison to his private apartment at the top of the tower'. Paris is not named, so the quiz answer holds. Minor: it is now open to the public, so FR 'se cache' is licence, not error. 86/82 chars.

hooks.en: A father proved the electron is a particle. His son proved it is a wave. Both were right.
hooks.fr: Le père : une particule. Le fils : une onde. Les deux avaient raison sur l'électron.
hooks.note: J. J. Thomson (1897, cathode rays as particles) and G. P. Thomson (1927, electron interference through foils) are both in the article; the father-son link is on their own pages. 'Proved it is a wave' is the standard textbook shorthand and is defused by 'both were right'. FR is fragmentary and non-calqued; 'les deux avaient raison' is colloquial rather than wrong. 88/83 chars.

hooks.en: The poem is still not finished. Software is hunting its missing lines in museum drawers.
hooks.fr: Le poème est toujours incomplet. Des logiciels traquent ses vers perdus dans les musées.
hooks.note: Verified: 'the epic remains incomplete' (about a third of the 12-tablet Standard Babylonian version still missing) and 'recent developments in the use of artificial intelligence software have vastly accelerated the process of uncovering new fragments... dispersed, and often unread, in museums around the world'. Quiz answer (Mesopotamia) untouched. 87/87 chars.

hooks.en: Zero on this scale was a bucket of ice and salt. 96 was meant to be body temperature.
hooks.fr: Son zéro : un mélange de glace et de sel. Et 96 devait être la température du corps.
hooks.note: Verified: 0 was 'a mixture of ice, water and salis Armoniaci' (ammonium chloride — a salt); 96 was body temperature on his original scale, only becoming 98.6 after the 1776-77 recalibration. Does not touch the quiz answer (-40). The unexplained 96 is what pulls. 84/83 chars.

hooks.en: The harbour was chained shut. So how did the sultan's fleet get in?
hooks.fr: Le port était fermé par une chaîne. Comment la flotte du sultan est-elle entrée ?
hooks.note: Verified: the Golden Horn chain 'was strong enough to prevent any Turkish ship from entering the harbour'; Mehmed built 'a road of greased logs across Galata... and dragged his ships over the hill' on 22 April. The city is not named, so the quiz answer holds. Answer is genuinely unguessable — best-pulling hook in the slice. 66/80 chars.

hooks.en: Hand a forensic scientist this one bone and they can tell you your height.
hooks.fr: Donnez cet os à un légiste : il vous dira quelle taille vous faisiez.
hooks.note: FAILED pulls — generic. 'This bone is not solid, part of what is inside makes your blood' is true but works verbatim for the humerus, tibia or any long bone, and it states its own payoff. Replaced with a femur-specific claim from the article: 'the femur length accounts for 26.74% of a person's height... it provides a reliable estimate of a person's height from an incomplete skeleton'. Avoids 'thigh', which would have leaked the quiz answer ('in the leg'). 73/68 chars.

hooks.en: A sequence from a medieval rabbit puzzle keeps reappearing in pine cones.
hooks.fr: Une suite née d'un problème de lapins réapparaît dans les pommes de pin.

hooks.en: Settling this flag took six months of debate and a vote at 2 a.m.
hooks.fr: Six mois de débats, puis un vote à deux heures du matin : voilà comment ce drapeau est né.
hooks.note: FAILED truthful — the 308 figure is disputed inside Wikipedia itself: Flag of Canada says '308 speeches', Great Canadian Flag Debate says 'after some 250 speeches'. A contested number stated as fact is a defect. Kept the six months, which is solid (parliamentary phase 15 June - 15 December 1964), and swapped in the verified detail that 'the final vote adopting the Stanley flag took place at 2:15 on the morning of December 15, 1964'. Country still unnamed, so the quiz answer holds. 64/89 chars.

hooks.en: The oldest tellings of this legend have no snake in them at all. Where did it come from?
hooks.fr: Les plus anciennes versions de la légende ne comportent aucun serpent. D'où sort-il ?
hooks.note: Verified on Coat of arms of Mexico (the Flag of Mexico article does not cover it): the Codex Mendoza and other early sources 'show only an eagle'; the serpent 'was derived from an incorrect translation' of ihuan cohuatl izomocayan, possibly confused with the atl-tlachinolli war glyph. Centres the Mexica telling and puts the European addition in question — clean on the decolonial rubric. Mexico not named. 87/84 chars.

hooks.en: Until 1962 the sun and the moon on this flag had human faces.
hooks.fr: Jusqu'en 1962, le soleil et la lune de ce drapeau avaient un visage humain.
hooks.note: Verified verbatim: 'Until 1962, the flag's emblems, both the sun and the crescent moon, had human faces, but they were removed to modernise the flag'; current flag adopted 16 December 1962. Nepal is not named, so the quiz answer (two stacked triangles) holds. 60/74 chars.

hooks.en: Why did Kahlo insist she was born three years after she actually was?
hooks.fr: Pourquoi Kahlo s'est-elle rajeunie de trois ans toute sa vie ?
hooks.note: FAILED fr_ok — 'née trois ans après sa vraie naissance' is a clumsy calque; 'sa vraie naissance' is not French usage. Replaced with the standard idiom 'se rajeunir de trois ans', which carries the same pull in fewer words. EN verified and unchanged: born 6 July 1907, claimed 7 July 1910, 'the year the Mexican Revolution began'. Quiz answer (self-portraits) untouched. 69/61 chars.

hooks.en: One of nature's four forces gets stronger the further you pull it apart.
hooks.fr: L'une des quatre forces fondamentales se renforce quand on l'étire. Laquelle ?
hooks.note: FAILED truthful — 'nothing it binds can ever be pulled apart' is false as written. The same interaction binds nucleons through its residual effect ('it creates the nuclear force that binds the latter particles to form atomic nuclei'), and nuclei are split routinely; confinement applies to quarks, not to everything the strong force binds. Rewrite keeps only what the article states outright: 'the strong force increases indefinitely with distance'. Gravity, the quiz answer, is still not mentioned. 71/77 chars.

hooks.en: One aquifer under this desert holds more water than the entire Persian Gulf.
hooks.fr: Une seule nappe sous ce désert contient plus d'eau que tout le golfe Persique.
hooks.note: Checkable verbatim: 'the Wasia, the largest aquifer in Saudi Arabia, contains more water than the Persian Gulf'. Flag for the record: that line traces to the 1992 US Library of Congress country study, so it is an old estimate — but it is stated flatly in the topic's own article and the hook does not sharpen it. The Persian Gulf appears in the quiz question, not its answer (Saudi Arabia), so nothing leaks. 75/77 chars.

hooks.en: A new country chose the name of an empire that never stood on its land.
hooks.fr: Un pays neuf a pris le nom d'un empire qui n'a jamais occupé son territoire.

hooks.en: Every gold nugget belonged to the king by law. Everyone else could own only the dust.
hooks.fr: Toute pépite d'or revenait au roi. Aux autres, la poussière d'or seulement.
hooks.note: Verified from al-Bakri via the article: 'The king claimed as his own all nuggets of gold, and allowed other people to have only gold dust.' The hook withholds the reason (holding the gold price up), which is exactly the gap. Salt, the quiz answer, is not mentioned. 'By law' is a fair gloss on a royal prerogative. 84/74 chars.

hooks.en: Almost all of Earth's gold sank into the core. So what are we digging up?
hooks.fr: Presque tout l'or de la Terre a sombré dans le noyau. Alors, que déterre-t-on ?
hooks.note: FAILED truthful — 'made by dying stars' states a contested mechanism as settled. The article lists three cosmic sources (supernova nucleosynthesis, neutron star collisions, magnetar flares) and says the emphasis has shifted to neutron star collisions, which are mergers of dead remnants, not dying stars. Rewrite uses two flat statements from the same article: 'almost all of the gold present in the early Earth probably sank into the planetary core' and 'most of the gold in the Earth's crust and mantle is thought to have been delivered to Earth by asteroid impacts'. It also pulls harder — the old line informed rather than opened anything. 72/78 chars.

hooks.en: You weigh least on a mountain in Peru, and most on the Arctic Ocean.
hooks.fr: C'est sur une montagne du Pérou que vous pesez le moins. Et le plus, sur l'océan Arctique.
hooks.note: FAILED spoiler — the hook printed 'the Equator', which is the quiz answer verbatim. Every other hook in the bank avoids the answer string ('this river', 'this flag'); this one broke that. The Huascarán claim itself is exact: 'from 9.7639 m/s2 on the Nevado Huascarán mountain in Peru to 9.8337 m/s2 at the surface of the Arctic Ocean'. Rewrite swaps the Equator foil for the Arctic Ocean pole of the same sentence — the paradox survives, the answer no longer appears. 67/88 chars.

hooks.en: How do whole reefs, spread over kilometres, all spawn on the very same nights?
hooks.fr: Comment des récifs entiers, étalés sur des kilomètres, pondent-ils tous les mêmes nuits ?
hooks.note: FAILED truthful — 'an entire reef... on the same night, every year' is contradicted by the article: 'Reefs in the inner Great Barrier Reef spawn during the week after the full moon in October, while the outer reefs spawn in November and December.' It is not one night, and not reef-system-wide. Rewrite scales the claim to what is supported (mass spawning events synchronised within a reef, triggered by temperature, the lunar cycle and the diurnal cycle) and keeps the how-do-they-coordinate gap. Also dropped a draft line about corals not seeing — they do sense moonlight, which is the mechanism. 77/88 chars.

hooks.en: A constitution centuries older than the United States, and not written on paper.
hooks.fr: Une constitution bien plus ancienne que les États-Unis, et pas écrite sur du papier.

hooks.en: This building would dissolve in the rain if the whole town didn't show up.
hooks.fr: Ce bâtiment fondrait sous la pluie si toute la ville ne venait pas chaque année.

hooks.en: Its four sides find true north to within a tenth of a degree. Nobody had a compass.
hooks.fr: Ses quatre faces visent le nord vrai à un dixième de degré près. Sans boussole.
hooks.note: VERIFIED. Wikipedia: sides of the base deviate 'on average 3 minutes and 38 seconds of arc, or about a tenth of a degree' — so 'within a tenth of a degree' is accurate and conservative (0.06°). Quiz (which wonder still stands) untouched. Strong pull: the second sentence removes the obvious explanation. 17 words is slightly over the ~14 guidance but 82 chars and reads in two beats; kept unchanged per the pass rule.

hooks.en: The mortar holding the Ming walls together was mixed with something you could eat.
hooks.fr: Le mortier des murailles Ming contient un ingrédient qui se mange. Lequel ?
hooks.note: VERIFIED. Wikipedia Great Wall: 'Sticky rice mortar, consisting of sticky rice soup mixed with slaked lime, was extensively used to hold bricks together.' Ming attribution correct. Quiz answer (China) not named. FR returned with espace insécable before '?'.

hooks.en: Rhodesia's government censored archaeologists who said Africans built this city.
hooks.fr: Le régime rhodésien censurait les archéologues qui l'attribuaient à des Africains.
hooks.note: VERIFIED, and the strongest decolonial hook in the slice. Wikipedia: 'The official line in Rhodesia during the 1960s and 1970s was that the structures were built by non-blacks. Archaeologists who disputed the official statement were censored by the government' — plus Sinclair's testimony and Garlake's/Summers's departures. Not a spoiler: quiz answer is 'Zimbabwe', the hook says 'Rhodesia'. FR: the elided 'l'' leans on the card's topic title for its antecedent — acceptable in headline register, worth watching if card layout ever changes.

hooks.en: An early Taoist text warns alchemists never to mix these powders. Houses had burned down.
hooks.fr: Un texte taoïste met en garde : ne mélangez jamais ces poudres. Des maisons y sont passées.
hooks.note: VERIFIED. Zhenyuan miaodao yaolüe (c. mid-9th c.): 'Some have heated together sulfur, realgar and saltpeter with honey; smoke [and flames] result, so that their hands and faces have been burnt, and even the whole house burned down.' The warning addresses multiple practitioners, so plural 'Houses' is faithful. Borderline note for the CoS: 'Taoist' is an indirect pointer to the quiz answer (China), but it is not the answer word and does not restate the question — not scored as a spoiler.

hooks.en: The web's own protocol gives the server no memory of you. Yet sites know you anyway.
hooks.fr: Le web repose sur un protocole sans mémoire. Comment les sites vous reconnaissent-ils ?
hooks.note: FIXED — overstated as written. 'The server has forgotten who you are' is literally false for any logged-in session: servers do remember, via cookies and sessions. Wikipedia HTTP is precise about the layer: 'As a stateless protocol, HTTP does not require the web server to retain information or status about each user for the duration of multiple requests.' Rewrite moves the claim to the protocol (true) and keeps the pull by naming the paradox. FR rewritten around the same tension, espace insécable before '?'.

hooks.en: In 1504 a king turned against this alphabet: someone had criticised him in it.
hooks.fr: En 1504, un roi s'en prend à cet alphabet : on l'y avait critiqué.
hooks.note: FIXED — rounded number stated as fact. Hangul was promulgated 1446 (introduced 1443); Yeonsangun's persecution was 1504, i.e. 58 years later, not 'sixty'. A hard date is both true and more concrete. Also softened 'insulted' to 'criticised': Wikipedia says he acted 'after learning that criticisms of him had been written in the script'. Not a spoiler — the quiz answer is Sejong, and this is a different, later king.

hooks.en: As a child, at an altar, he was made to swear he would never be a friend of Rome.
hooks.fr: Enfant, devant l'autel, on lui fit jurer de n'être jamais l'ami de Rome.
hooks.note: PASS with a flag for the record. The oath rests on Polybius (Hannibal's own later telling to Antiochus) and Livy — Wikipedia presents it as 'According to Polybius…', not as documented fact. The hook is careful: it uses Polybius's actual wording ('never to be a friend of the Romans') rather than the inflated 'eternal hatred' version, and it avoids the disputed age of nine. Britannica states it flatly too. Kept unchanged; if the CoS wants zero source-attribution risk anywhere in the bank, this is the one to revisit.

hooks.en: A club of merchant towns went to war with the King of Denmark. The towns won.
hooks.fr: Une ligue de villes marchandes a fait la guerre au roi du Danemark. Et l'a gagnée.
hooks.note: VERIFIED. Danish–Hanseatic War (1361–70): the Confederation of Cologne 'sacked Copenhagen and Helsingborg, and forced Valdemar IV, King of Denmark… to grant tax exemptions and influence over Øresund fortresses' at the Treaty of Stralsund, 1370. Towns did win the decisive phase. Quiz answer (Lübeck) not touched. 'Club' carries the tension: no state, no king, and it beat one.

hooks.en: Nothing tells your heart to beat. It makes its own electricity.
hooks.fr: Rien n'ordonne à votre cœur de battre : il fabrique lui-même son électricité.
hooks.note: VERIFIED. Cardiac autorhythmicity: the sinoatrial node generates the impulse; a denervated transplanted heart still beats. The autonomic nervous system modulates rate but does not initiate it, so 'nothing tells it to beat' is the standard and defensible framing, not an overstatement. Quiz (four chambers) untouched. FR espace insécable before ':'.

hooks.en: A cow does not digest grass. Something else living inside it does that work.
hooks.fr: Une vache ne digère pas l'herbe. D'autres organismes, à l'intérieur, s'en chargent pour elle.

hooks.en: Before 'hexadecimal', this system had another name. It was quietly dropped.
hooks.fr: Avant « hexadécimal », ce système portait un autre nom. On l'a discrètement abandonné.
hooks.note: VERIFIED. Wikipedia: 'The all-Latin alternative sexadecimal… is older, and sees at least occasional use from the late 19th century. It is still in use in the 1950s in Bendix documentation', and 'Schwartzman (1994) argues that use of sexadecimal may have been avoided because of its suggestive abbreviation to sex.' 'Quietly dropped' matches the hedged sourcing without asserting the reason. FR: espaces insécables inside « ».

hooks.en: A retreating Greek army ate the local honey. Nobody could stand up for days.
hooks.fr: Une armée grecque en retraite mangea le miel du coin. Plus personne ne tenait debout.
hooks.note: FIXED — the date is probably wrong by a year. Wikipedia's Mad honey article says 401 BCE, but that is the year of Cunaxa and the start of the march; the honey episode falls in Anabasis 4.8.20, just before the Ten Thousand reached Trapezus, which was early 400 BCE. Per the spec ('if you are not certain, rewrite around something you ARE certain of') I removed the year rather than ship a contested one. The incapacitation is solid: Xenophon has them recovering their senses the next day and getting up 'on the third and fourth days'. Quiz (honey never spoils) untouched.

hooks.en: A returning bee dances on the comb. The angle of her dance is a map.
hooks.fr: Une butineuse rentre et danse sur le rayon. L'angle de sa danse est une carte.
hooks.note: VERIFIED. Waggle dance: 'flowers located directly in line with the sun are represented by waggle runs in an upward direction on the vertical combs, and any angle to the right or left of the sun is coded by a corresponding angle…'. 'Her' is correct — all foragers are workers, i.e. female. 'Is a map' states that direction is encoded without revealing how, so the gap stays open. FR 'butineuse' is native usage, not a translation.

hooks.en: Some Greek works survive only because someone in Baghdad translated them. The originals are gone.
hooks.fr: Certains textes grecs n'existent plus qu'en arabe : l'original a disparu, la traduction non.

hooks.en: About a thousand species of bacteria live on your skin. Hardly any harm you.
hooks.fr: Environ mille espèces de bactéries vivent sur votre peau. Presque aucune ne vous nuit.
hooks.note: FIXED — second sentence overstated, first sentence rounded. Wikipedia Skin flora: ~1,000 species from nineteen phyla, and 'Skin flora is usually non-pathogenic, and either commensal (are not harmful to their host) or mutualistic (offer a benefit)'. Most are commensal (neutral), not actively 'defending' — that claim overreaches the source. Added 'About' since the source says approximately. The pull survives and arguably improves: if they are not harming you, what are a thousand species doing there?

hooks.en: Your body makes something harder than bone — and can never grow it back.
hooks.fr: Votre corps fabrique une matière plus dure que l'os. Il ne saura jamais la refaire.
hooks.note: FIXED — 'can never repair it' is contradicted by the source. Wikipedia Tooth enamel: enamel 'is the hardest substance in the human body' and 'has no way to regenerate itself', BUT limited early damage is repairable by remineralisation ('damage beyond that cannot be repaired by the body'). 'Grow it back' states the true, absolute part (no regeneration) without colliding with remineralisation. Quiz (32 teeth) untouched.

hooks.en: England lost in 1453. Its kings kept the title King of France for three more centuries.
hooks.fr: L'Angleterre perd en 1453. Ses rois se diront rois de France trois siècles de plus.
hooks.note: VERIFIED. George III dropped 'king of France' from the royal style in 1801, so the title outlived the defeat by 348 years — 'three more centuries' understates rather than overstates, which is the safe direction and literally true. Does not leak the quiz answer (116 years): it gives the end date only. FR uses narrative present + future, which is native register, not calque.

hooks.en: In the whole periodic table, one atom alone has no neutron. Why that one?
hooks.fr: Dans tout le tableau périodique, un seul atome ne contient aucun neutron. Pourquoi lui ?
hooks.note: FIXED — spoiler. The quiz asks 'What is the most abundant element in the universe?' (answer: Hydrogen) and the hook opened with 'The commonest atom in the universe' under a card titled Hydrogen: that is the question and its answer restated back at the reader. The neutron claim itself is sound — Wikipedia Isotopes of hydrogen: '1H… is the only stable nuclide with no neutrons' — so I kept the fact and dropped the abundance framing, then converted the flat statistic into a question to restore the pull.

hooks.en: He left home at twenty-one to make the pilgrimage. He was gone for twenty-four years.
hooks.fr: Parti à vingt et un ans pour le pèlerinage, il ne rentre que vingt-quatre ans plus tard.
hooks.note: VERIFIED, both numbers exact. Wikipedia: 'On 2 Rajab 725 AH (14 June 1325 AD), Ibn Battuta set off from his home town at the age of 21' and 'He would not return to Morocco again for 24 years.' Deliberately avoids the 117,000 km figure that is the quiz answer's own fact line. Gap opened: a hajj is months, so what happened to the other 23 years?

hooks.en: Physicists still do not agree on why ice is slippery.
hooks.fr: Pourquoi la glace glisse-t-elle ? Les physiciens n'ont toujours pas tranché.
hooks.note: VERIFIED. Wikipedia Ice: 'the mechanism controlling the frictional properties of ice is still an active area of scientific study', with the competing pressure-melting / frictional-heating / premelting accounts each noted as limited. Best pull in the slice — the gap is a genuine open question, so it cannot be closed in the reader's head. 52 chars. FR flips to question form natively; espace insécable before '?'.

hooks.en: Its bridges were woven from grass, and had to be rebuilt every other year.
hooks.fr: Ses ponts étaient tressés en herbe et devaient être refaits tous les deux ans.

hooks.en: Two Greek mathematicians tried to explain why a ramp helps. Both got it wrong.
hooks.fr: Pourquoi une rampe allège-t-elle l'effort ? Deux mathématiciens grecs s'y sont cassé les dents.
hooks.note: EN verified and unchanged: Wikipedia Inclined plane confirms Heron of Alexandria and Pappus of Alexandria both attempted the derivation and 'their solutions were incorrect' (first correct treatments: Jordanus de Nemore, then Varro/Stevin/Galileo in the 1580s–90s). FR FAILED: 'pourquoi la rampe aide' is an anglicism — 'aider' used absolutely does not work in French. Rewritten around a native construction and the idiom 's'y casser les dents', which carries 'both got it wrong' properly. 95 chars, espace insécable before '?'.

hooks.en: Sailors here waited for the wind to change direction. It always did, on schedule.
hooks.fr: Ici, les marins attendaient que le vent change de sens. Il le faisait, ponctuellement.

hooks.en: The cotton feeding the new mills was grown by enslaved people an ocean away.
hooks.fr: Le coton des nouvelles filatures était cultivé par des esclaves, un océan plus loin.
hooks.note: FIXED — spoiler only. The quiz answer is 'Great Britain' and the hook named Britain outright; deleting the possessive costs nothing because the card is already titled Industrial Revolution. Substance stands: Lancashire's mills ran overwhelmingly on slave-grown cotton, West Indian and Brazilian early on, then US Southern cotton dominant through the 19th century. Decolonially the strongest framing available for this topic — it names who actually paid for the machines. FR already avoided naming Britain, so it ships unchanged.

hooks.en: Eighteen of his plays survive only because two fellow actors printed them after his death.
hooks.fr: Sans deux comédiens, dix-huit de ses pièces auraient disparu avec lui.
hooks.note: FIXED — 'half' rounds up. Wikipedia First Folio: 36 plays, of which eighteen had never been printed before, compiled by John Heminges and Henry Condell, both King's Men (so 'fellow actors' is right). Eighteen is exactly half of the Folio but only ~46% of the ~39-play canon, and the hook said 'half his plays'. The precise number is also the better hook — it invites 'which eighteen?' where 'half' invites nothing.

hooks.en: Insects have no lungs. That single fact caps how big any of them can get.
hooks.fr: Les insectes n'ont pas de poumons. Cela suffit à plafonner leur taille.
hooks.note: PASS, with a caveat logged. Wikipedia Insect states both halves flatly: 'Insect respiration is accomplished without lungs' and 'The respiratory system limits the size of insects.' So the hook clears the checkable-against-Wikipedia bar. Caveat for the CoS: 'that single fact' asserts sole causation, and the literature also weighs Palaeozoic oxygen levels, moulting mechanics and (Clapham & Karr 2012) competition from birds. Not scored as a defect because the cited source is unhedged, but this is the weakest truth claim among the passes.

hooks.en: The biggest stars fuse their way up the periodic table — until they hit iron. Then they die.
hooks.fr: Les grandes étoiles fusionnent les éléments jusqu'au fer. Ensuite, elles meurent.
hooks.note: VERIFIED. Wikipedia Iron: iron-56 is 'the most common endpoint of nucleosynthesis' and 'the endpoint of fusion chains inside extremely massive stars'; 'elements heavier than iron require a supernova for their formation'. Fusion past iron consumes energy, hence core collapse — 'then they die' is correct for massive stars. Naming iron is not a spoiler: the card is titled Iron, so the quiz answer (Fe = iron) is already on screen. 91 chars; 17 words is over the ~14 guidance but the em-dash splits it into two beats, so kept unchanged per the pass rule.

hooks.en: In everyday speech people rarely used this city's name. They just said 'the City'.
hooks.fr: Au quotidien, on prononçait rarement son nom : on disait « la Ville », et tous comprenaient.
hooks.note: FIXED — absolute claim the source does not support. Wikipedia Names of Istanbul: 'In popular speech, the most common way of referring to it came to be simply the City (hē Polis)' — most common in speech, not 'people did not use this city's name'. Constantinople was used constantly in documents, coinage and law, so the flat negative is refutable by any Byzantinist. Narrowed to 'in everyday speech… rarely', which is exactly what the source says and keeps the whole pull. FR: espace insécable before ':' and inside « ».

hooks.en: He defined horsepower to sell steam engines — by timing a real horse at a mill wheel.
hooks.fr: Il a défini le cheval-vapeur pour vendre ses machines, en chronométrant un vrai cheval.
hooks.note: VERIFIED, both halves. Wikipedia Horsepower: 'The idea was later used by James Watt to help market the Watt steam engine' (his royalty-on-coal-savings scheme failed against customers still using horses), and 'Watt determined that a horse could turn a mill wheel 144 times in an hour (or 2.4 times a minute)' — a rate measured at a mill wheel, which is what 'timing a real horse' describes. Minor caveat: the source does not say he stopwatched one specific animal, and a rival brewery-horse anecdote circulates; the mill-wheel derivation is the sourced one, so the hook is safe as written.

hooks.en: Two monks brought the secret of silk to his court, hidden inside hollow canes.
hooks.fr: Deux moines rapportèrent à sa cour le secret de la soie, caché dans des cannes creuses.
hooks.note: Verified: Wikipedia 'Smuggling of silkworm eggs into the Byzantine Empire' — two unidentified monks, eggs concealed in their bamboo canes, c.552, presented as history not legend. Never names Justinian, so the quiz answer stays intact. Unchanged.

hooks.en: Local tradition says seven visits to this mosque equal one pilgrimage to Mecca.
hooks.fr: Sept visites à cette mosquée valent un pèlerinage à La Mecque, dit la tradition.
hooks.note: Verified verbatim: Kairouan article — 'Local tradition holds that seven pilgrimages to the Great Mosque equals one pilgrimage to Mecca.' Correctly attributed to tradition rather than asserted as doctrine, which is the difference between a fact and a defect here. City name withheld. Unchanged.

hooks.en: One mother produces two different milks at the same time, from different teats.
hooks.fr: Une mère produit deux laits différents en même temps, par deux mamelles distinctes.
hooks.note: Verified: Kangaroo article — 'the mother is able to produce two different kinds of milk simultaneously for the new-born and the older joey still in the pouch.' Does not use the word 'joey', so the quiz answer is safe. Unchanged.

hooks.en: We know the exact year the Norse cut this timber: 1021. Tree rings gave it away.
hooks.fr: On connaît l'année exacte où les Vikings ont coupé ce bois : 1021. Les cernes l'ont dit.
hooks.note: Verified: 1021 comes from radiocarbon on three tree-ring samples keyed to the 993 CE atmospheric 14C anomaly (Nature 2021), as stated in the article. Naming 'tree rings' teases the method without explaining how a single calendar year can be recovered — the gap stays open. Does not touch the answer (Scandinavia). NBSP added before the colon.

hooks.en: Why do the wealthy here live at the bottom of the city, not on the heights?
hooks.fr: Pourquoi les riches vivent-ils ici en bas de la ville, et non sur les hauteurs ?
hooks.note: Verified: La Paz article — 'The more affluent residents live in the lower, central areas of the city southwest of the Prado'; 'Lower-income residents live in makeshift brick houses in the surrounding hills.' Inverts a reader's default expectation, which is exactly the pull. Unchanged; NBSP before '?'.

hooks.en: Seals live in this lake. Nobody is sure how they got here from the sea.
hooks.fr: Des phoques vivent dans ce lac. Personne ne sait comment ils y sont arrivés.
hooks.note: Verified: the Baikal seal article offers only competing hypotheses (swimming up rivers in prehistory, or an ancient link via the Paratethys / West Siberian Glacial Lake). The origin is genuinely unresolved, and both hypotheses are marine, so 'from the sea' is not an unsupported presupposition. Unchanged.

hooks.en: A predatory fish was introduced here to boost the catch. Around 200 native species are gone.
hooks.fr: Un poisson prédateur, lâché ici pour doper la pêche : environ 200 espèces locales ont disparu.
hooks.note: FIXED — the date was not safe. The Lake Victoria article places the 1954 release upstream of Murchison Falls (not in the lake) and the transfers into Victoria itself at 1962–63; the Nile perch article says loosely 'the 1950s'. Wikipedia contradicts itself, so the decade is dropped rather than shipped. Species figure kept and is conservative: 'at least 200 species (about 40 percent) of Lake Victoria haplochromines have become extinct'. Replacing the date with the motive ('to boost the catch') also strengthens the pull — the reader now wants the fish and the irony.

hooks.en: The world's most populous landlocked country had a coastline within living memory.
hooks.fr: Le pays enclavé le plus peuplé du monde avait encore une côte à la fin du XXe siècle.
hooks.note: Verified: 'Ethiopia is the world's most populous landlocked country' (verbatim), made landlocked by Eritrean independence in 1993 — comfortably within living memory and within 'la fin du XXe siècle'. Names no country, so the doubly-landlocked answer (Uzbekistan) is untouched. Strongest pull in the slice. Unchanged.

hooks.en: Part of this North African city now stands in an English royal park.
hooks.fr: Une partie de cette cité africaine se dresse aujourd'hui dans un parc royal anglais.

hooks.en: Why does South Africa pay this mountain kingdom to send its water downhill?
hooks.fr: Pourquoi l'Afrique du Sud paie-t-elle ce royaume de montagne pour son eau ?
hooks.note: Verified: Lesotho Highlands Water Project — royalties of R780 million (2015), about 5% of Lesotho's non-tax state income; water descends by gravity through the transfer and delivery tunnels, so 'downhill' is literal. 'South Africa' is in the quiz stem already, so naming it spoils nothing. Unchanged; NBSP before '?'.

hooks.en: Astronomers writing for each other rarely use light-years. They prefer a bigger unit.
hooks.fr: Entre eux, les astronomes n'emploient guère l'année-lumière. Ils ont une unité plus grande.
hooks.note: REWRITTEN — failed three checks. Truth: (1) the nearest star is the Sun; (2) '45 million years by car' hides an unstated speed — 100 km/h gives ~46m years, 120 km/h gives ~38m, so the figure is not checkable as written. Spoiler: 'four light-years off' plus 'the drive' hands back the quiz answer (a light-year is a unit of distance). Pull: it was a closed wow-stat with nothing left to ask. Replacement is verbatim-sourced from the topic article — 'The unit most commonly used in professional astronomy is the parsec (pc), approximately 3.26 light-years' — is true, says 'unit' without saying 'distance', and leaves which unit and why wide open.

hooks.en: Lions are not only African. A wild population survives in one Indian state.
hooks.fr: Le lion n'est pas qu'africain : une population sauvage subsiste dans un seul État indien.
hooks.note: FIXED — 'one forest' is out of date and now materially wrong. May 2025 census: 891 Asiatic lions over 35,000 km² spanning 11 districts, with only 394 in Gir National Park and adjoining areas and 507 in nine satellite populations. All of them are still in Gujarat, so 'one Indian state' is exact, ages better, and loses none of the pull. Does not touch the answer (pride).

hooks.en: More than half of all your bones are in your hands and feet. Why so many?
hooks.fr: Plus de la moitié de vos os se trouvent dans vos mains et vos pieds. Pourquoi ?
hooks.note: Arithmetic checked against the topic article: 27 bones per hand (8+5+14) x2 = 54, 26 per foot (7+5+14) x2 = 52, total 106 of 206 = 51.5%. 'More than half' is true by a real margin, not a rounding. Never states 206, so the quiz answer survives. Unchanged; NBSP before '?'.

hooks.en: The world's most populous island doesn't even make the top ten by size.
hooks.fr: L'île la plus peuplée du monde n'est même pas dans les dix plus vastes.
hooks.note: Verified against the topic article's own table: Java is 13th at 127,467 km², well outside the top ten (10th is Ellesmere at 197,790 km²), and Java is the world's most populous island. Australia is excluded there as a continent, which is consistent with the quiz answer without restating it. Unchanged.

hooks.en: Quechua families were already farming these terraces when its 'discoverer' arrived.
hooks.fr: Des familles quechuas cultivaient déjà ces terrasses quand son « découvreur » est arrivé.
hooks.note: Verified: 'a small hut occupied by a couple of Quechua people, Richarte and Alvarez, who were farming some of the original Machu Picchu agricultural terraces that they had cleared four years earlier' — plus Richarte's 11-year-old son, so 'families' holds. Best decolonial compliance in the slice: names the people whose place it is and quarantines 'discoverer'. 'Quechua' is not the quiz answer word ('Inca'). Unchanged; NBSP inside the guillemets.

hooks.en: The design team signed the inside of the case, where no owner would ever look.
hooks.fr: L'équipe a signé l'intérieur du boîtier, là où aucun acheteur ne regarderait jamais.
hooks.note: Verified verbatim: 'The original Macintosh includes the signatures of the Macintosh Division mostly as of early 1982 molded on the inside of the case.' Never says Apple. Unchanged.

hooks.en: Of its sixty-three clauses, three are still law in England. The rest are gone.
hooks.fr: Sur ses soixante-trois articles, trois sont encore en vigueur. Lesquels ?
hooks.note: Verified: 63 clauses in the 1215 charter; three survive in force in England and Wales via the 1297 reissue (Wikipedia: 'three clauses of the original charter are enshrined in the 1297 reissued Magna Carta and do still remain in force in England and Wales'; UK Parliament agrees). 'Still law in England' is accurate and not overstated. The 63-to-3 collapse carries the 'wait, why' — thin but real, and the FR sharpens it with 'Lesquels ?'. Unchanged; NBSP before '?'.

hooks.en: An empire named after a fruit — because the first settlers found it bitter.
hooks.fr: Un empire qui doit son nom à un fruit : les premiers défricheurs l'ont trouvé amer.
hooks.note: EN verified and unchanged: the maja fruit (Aegle marmelos) plus pahit, 'bitter' — 'the workers clearing the Trik forest encountered some maja trees and consumed their bitter-tasting fruit which then gave its name to the village.' FR failed: 'les premiers venus' collides with the fixed French idiom 'le premier venu' (= any Tom, Dick or Harry), so it reads as a mistranslation rather than as 'the first arrivals'. 'Les premiers défricheurs' is idiomatic and closer to the source. Java is never named.

hooks.en: He said his predecessor sailed west into the Atlantic with 2,000 ships and never returned.
hooks.fr: Selon son récit, son prédécesseur partit vers l'ouest avec 2 000 navires. On ne l'a jamais revu.
hooks.note: Verified: al-Umari's report of Musa's own account — 200 ships on the first exploratory expedition, 2,000 on the second, which the predecessor led personally and never returned from. The 'He said' / 'Selon son récit' framing is load-bearing and correct: modern historians doubt the story and suspect Musa deposed him. Attributed claim, not asserted fact. Unchanged; NBSP as the FR thousands separator.

hooks.en: Her notebooks are still radioactive. You need protective clothing to read them.
hooks.fr: Ses carnets sont toujours radioactifs : il faut une tenue de protection pour les consulter.
hooks.note: Verified verbatim: 'her papers from the 1890s are considered too dangerous to handle... Her papers are kept in lead-lined boxes, and those who wish to consult them must wear protective clothing.' Uses 'Her', never the name, so the quiz answer holds. Unchanged; NBSP before the colon.

hooks.en: UNESCO protects a square in this city — not for its buildings, but for its storytellers.
hooks.fr: L'UNESCO protège ici une place, non pour ses murs mais pour ses conteurs.
hooks.note: Verified: Jemaa el-Fnaa was proclaimed a Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity in 2001 and listed in 2008 — the designation is for the oral tradition, explicitly not the architecture. City name withheld. Unchanged.

hooks.en: He fought for Carthage first. Then his cavalry hit Hannibal's rear at Zama and ended it.
hooks.fr: Il servit d'abord Carthage. Puis, à Zama, sa cavalerie prit Hannibal à revers et tout bascula.
hooks.note: REWRITTEN — 'finished Hannibal at Zama' reads as killed him; Hannibal survived Zama and lived to 183 BCE. The French was worse: 'acheva Hannibal' states it outright ('achever' = finish off, kill). The underlying credit is real and stays: he commanded 6,000 Numidian and 3,000 Roman cavalry, and 'Masinissa's cavalry... returned and immediately fell onto the rear of the Carthaginian lines. This decided the battle.' Side-switching is confirmed (fought for Carthage against Syphax early in the Second Punic War). Numidia is never named.

hooks.en: Heat a cup of coffee and it weighs more. Not by much, but genuinely more.
hooks.fr: Chauffez une tasse de café : elle pèse plus lourd. À peine — mais vraiment.
hooks.note: Verified verbatim: 'Raising the temperature of an object (increasing its thermal energy) increases its mass.' The hedge 'not by much' is honest — a 250 g cup heated 80 °C gains roughly a nanogram. Says nothing about c. Unchanged; NBSP before the colon.

hooks.en: A Soviet linguist found the key, having never seen a Maya site. The West dismissed him.
hooks.fr: Un linguiste soviétique en a trouvé la clé sans avoir vu de site maya. L'Occident l'a rejeté.
hooks.note: REWRITTEN — two truth defects. 'Without ever seeing a Maya ruin' is false as an absolute: Knorozov visited Tikal in 1990 at the invitation of President Cerezo. And 'cracked this script' overstates — he supplied the key (the syllabic approach and the synharmony principle); Proskouriakoff, Lounsbury and others completed the decipherment over decades. The new wording scopes 'never seen' to the moment of the discovery and says 'found the key'. The dismissal is well sourced and stays: Thompson 'led the attack', and progress accelerated only after his death in 1975. 'Maya' already appears in the topic name, so it is not a spoiler.

hooks.en: Plymouth was not built on empty ground. The village already there had a name.
hooks.fr: Plymouth ne fut pas bâtie sur une terre vide : le village d'avant avait un nom.

hooks.en: Closest to the Sun, and still not the hottest planet. Why not?
hooks.fr: La plus proche du Soleil, et pourtant pas la plus chaude. Pourquoi ?

hooks.en: Nobody has ever photographed our galaxy from outside. So how do we know?
hooks.fr: Personne n'a jamais photographié notre galaxie de l'extérieur. Comment la connaît-on ?

hooks.en: Part of every one of your cells was once something else entirely.
hooks.fr: Une partie de chacune de vos cellules fut autrefois un être à part entière.

hooks.en: How do you move a statue of many tonnes with no wheels or animals?
hooks.fr: Comment déplacer une statue de plusieurs tonnes sans roue ni animal de trait ?

hooks.en: The thief who walked out with it in 1911 had helped build its glass case.
hooks.fr: En 1911, le grand public n'y prêtait guère attention. Puis elle a disparu du Louvre.
hooks.note: en verified verbatim: Wikipedia says Peruggia 'had helped construct the painting's glass case'. Old fr failed twice: (1) Wikipedia says fame only 'partly stem[s] from its 1911 theft' — 'qu'après' asserts sole cause; (2) the painting was gone 21 Aug 1911 to 4 Jan 1914, over two years four months, not 'deux ans'. New fr rests on the article's exact line 'In 1911, the painting was still not popular among the lay-public' and takes a different angle from en. 84 chars.

hooks.en: Before this browser, a picture on a web page opened in a window of its own.
hooks.fr: Ses créateurs sont partis fonder le concurrent qui allait le faire disparaître.
hooks.note: No quiz for this slug, so no spoiler risk. en is article-supported ('the first browser to display images inline with text instead of a separate window') — but flag for the card body: some historians credit ViolaWWW with inline images first, so do not harden this beyond the hook. fr failed truth: 'en deux ans' is in no source. Wikipedia says decline began after Navigator's 1994 release and the project ran to Jan 1997. Number removed; French was already idiomatic. 79 chars.

hooks.en: The rock at the very top of the world holds fossils of sea creatures.
hooks.fr: Comment des fossiles marins se retrouvent-ils au sommet du monde ?
hooks.note: Verified: the summit unit is the Ordovician Qomolangma Formation, a marine limestone; trilobite, crinoid and ostracod fragments identified by Sakai et al. from rock collected 6 m below the summit. Quiz answer is China — untouched. fr is the same angle as en but natively phrased as a question; acceptable.

hooks.en: Women were barred from this mountain until 1872. One had climbed it in 1832.
hooks.fr: Au-dessus de la 8e station, le sommet du Fuji fait partie du domaine d'un sanctuaire.
hooks.note: Both dates verified on the Mount Fuji article: the 1872 Grand Council of State Edict 98 abolished female exclusion; 'Tatsu Takayama was the first woman on record to summit Mount Fuji in the fall of 1832'. Note the hook wisely does not claim she climbed in disguise — Wikipedia does not say so. fr fact sits on the Fujisan Hongu Sengen Taisha article ('the entire top of Mount Fuji from the 8th stage upwards is considered to be part of the shrine grounds'), so cite that page, not the Mount Fuji one. Quiz answer Japan is never named. fr is the softest puller in this slice but does open a real gap.

hooks.en: Tropical glaciers sit on this summit. Nearly 85% of the ice has gone since 1912.
hooks.fr: Ce volcan n'est pas éteint : des fumerolles s'échappent encore de son cratère.
hooks.note: Figure matches Wikipedia word for word: 'Almost 85 percent of the ice cover on Kilimanjaro disappeared between October 1912 and June 2011' — 'nearly 85%' is exact, not rounded up, and the loss has only grown since. fr verified: 'Kibo is dormant and could erupt again' and 'Kibo still has gas-emitting fumaroles in its crater'. Topic name never given away. The second en sentence is closer to a statistic than a pull; the first sentence carries the tension, so it passes.

hooks.en: Why would a country set fire to twelve tons of its own ivory?
hooks.fr: Le parc n'est clôturé que sur trois côtés. Le quatrième reste ouvert. Pourquoi ?
hooks.note: en verified verbatim: 'In 1989, Kenyan President Daniel arap Moi burned twelve tons of ivory on a site within the park.' Kenya is never named, so the quiz answer holds. fr failed as a word-for-word rendering of the English question — the clearest calque in the slice. Replaced with a separately verified fact from the same article: 'It is fenced on three sides, whereas the open southern boundary allows migrating wildlife to move between the park and the adjacent Kitengela plains.' Two hooks now carry two facts. 80 chars.

hooks.en: Its parliament, cabinet and supreme court all sit in a city that is not the capital.
hooks.fr: Sa douzième province n'a été ni conquise ni achetée : elle a été fabriquée.
hooks.note: Contested superlative — held and replaced. Wikipedia does say 'the world's second largest exporter of food and agricultural products by value', but FAO 2024 data ranks Brazil second and the Netherlands third, and the ranking flips year to year. A superlative that needs re-checking every year is a maintenance liability in a permanent library. fr also mirrored en word for word.
