Replacements are stable and verified: Wikipedia calls Amsterdam 'the nominal capital' and states 'The Hague holds the seat of the States General, cabinet, and Supreme Court'; Flevoland is 'the twelfth and newest province of the Netherlands, established in 1986', its polders drained 1942/1957/1968. Note fr avoids re-treading the quiz's below-sea-level fact by leading on manufacture, not water. 84 and 75 chars.

hooks.en: Your bathroom scale cannot measure kilograms. It measures something else and converts.
hooks.fr: Votre pèse-personne est incapable de mesurer des kilos. Il mesure autre chose.
hooks.note: Physically correct: spring and load-cell bathroom scales measure force and divide by an assumed g to display mass. The claim is specific to bathroom scales — a balance beam does compare masses — so the wording is safe as written and must not be generalised to 'scales' in the card body. Points at force without naming the newton, so the quiz answer survives.

hooks.en: Upper Egypt sits at the bottom of the map. The river decided which end is up.
hooks.fr: Sur la carte, la Haute-Égypte est tout en bas. C'est le fleuve qui a tranché.

hooks.en: The most famous hammer blow in European history may never have happened.
hooks.fr: Le coup de marteau le plus célèbre d'Europe n'a peut-être jamais été donné.
hooks.note: The hedge is doing necessary work and must stay. Wikipedia: 'he may not have posted them on the door at all' — the nailing rests on Melanchthon's 1548 account, and Luther himself claimed he went through proper channels. Wittenberg, the quiz answer, is never named. fr mirrors en in content but 'donner un coup de marteau' is native French idiom, not calque.

hooks.en: Nearly half the nitrogen in your body was made usable inside a factory.
hooks.fr: Près de la moitié de l'azote de votre corps est passée par un procédé industriel.
hooks.note: Exact match to Wikipedia's Haber process article: 'Nearly 50% of the nitrogen found in human tissues originated from the Haber-Bosch process.' 'Nearly half' is the source's own hedge, not a round-up. The word nitrogen appears, but the card title is 'Nitrogen fixation' anyway and the hook never touches the tested fact (78% of the atmosphere), so no spoiler.

hooks.en: Many early mammals only came out at night. What was hunting in the daylight?
hooks.fr: Beaucoup de mammifères primitifs ne sortaient que la nuit. Qui chassait le jour ?
hooks.note: Passes, but with a constraint on the card body. 'Many' correctly hedges what Wikipedia frames as the nocturnal bottleneck hypothesis, and the question's presupposition is true — predatory dinosaurs were active by day. However the literature attributes mammalian nocturnality primarily to dinosaur dominance and competition, not predation alone, so the fact text underneath must say 'dinosaurs owned the daylight', not 'dinosaurs hunted them into the night'. The word 'nocturnal' is never used, so the quiz answer holds.

hooks.en: Earth has more than one North Pole, and one of them is drifting toward Siberia.
hooks.fr: La Terre a plusieurs pôles Nord. L'un d'eux dérive vers la Sibérie.
hooks.note: Verified: geographic, magnetic, geomagnetic and inaccessibility poles are distinct, and Wikipedia states the magnetic north pole 'is moving from Canada towards Siberia'. Deliberately carries no speed figure, which is right — the published rate has moved from 9 to 55 km/year and would date the hook. Quiz answer (Arctic Ocean) untouched.

hooks.en: More than forty of these pyramids were demolished by one treasure hunter in the 1830s.
hooks.fr: Plus de quarante de ces pyramides ont été détruites par un seul chasseur de trésors.
hooks.note: 'More than forty' is the article's own number, not an inflation: 'he is considered responsible for the destruction of over 40 pyramids', Giuseppe Ferlini, 1830s. Sudan is never named, so the quiz answer holds. Decolonial check passes — the destroyer is named as the agent, the pyramids as the victim.

hooks.en: The tallest stele here probably fell as it was raised. It has lain broken ever since.
hooks.fr: Le ramener en Éthiopie a demandé trois vols et la réfection d'une piste d'atterrissage.
hooks.note: fr fully verified and unchanged: the stele was cut in three and flown home on 19, 22 and 25 April 2005, and 'the runway at Axum airport was then upgraded specifically to facilitate the return of the stele'. en failed on hedging only — Wikipedia attributes the 33 m Great Stele's collapse to 'possibly immediately after their erection', a belief, and the original asserted it flatly. 'Probably fell as it was raised' matches the source and keeps the pull intact. Note the en is about a different stele from the topic's own obelisk; that contrast is deliberate, so the card body must make clear which is which. 84 chars.

hooks.en: Two thirds of this animal's neurons are nowhere near its brain.
hooks.fr: Les deux tiers de ses neurones ne sont pas dans sa tête. Où sont-ils donc ?
hooks.note: Verified verbatim: 'Two-thirds of the neurons are in the nerve cords of its arms'. The octopus brain sits in the head, so 'pas dans sa tête' is accurate as well as vivid. Never touches the three-hearts answer. fr adds its own question rather than translating en's full stop — good.

hooks.en: The hero of this epic is nowhere to be seen for its first four books.
hooks.fr: Le héros n'apparaît qu'au chant V. Que raconte-t-on pendant les quatre premiers ?
hooks.note: Wikipedia confirms 'Books 1 to 4, which focus on the perspective of Telemachus, are called the Telemachy'; Odysseus first appears on stage at Calypso's island in Book 5. He is discussed earlier but never seen, which is exactly what 'nowhere to be seen' claims. 'Chant V' is the correct French convention for the poem's books. Title never given away.

hooks.en: The law named after him got such a cold reception that he resigned his position.
hooks.fr: Sa loi fut si froidement accueillie qu'il démissionna de son poste.
hooks.note: Both halves are in the article and adjacent: 'it was coldly received at that time' and 'Ohm's college did not appreciate his work and Ohm resigned from his position.' The causal link is Wikipedia's own juxtaposition. No date is claimed, which is correct — the article gives none. The hook never names the unit, though the card title does.

hooks.en: Stand on this volcano's summit and you would not notice you were on a mountain.
hooks.fr: Au sommet de ce volcan, on ne s'apercevrait même pas qu'on est sur une montagne.
hooks.note: Verified almost verbatim: 'an observer near the summit would be unaware of standing on a very high mountain, as the slope of the volcano would extend far beyond the horizon, a mere 3 kilometres away'. Average flank slope 5%. Mars, the quiz answer, is never named. fr mirrors en but is natively phrased.

hooks.en: While he wrote it, his wife bought their food on credit and owed nine months' rent.
hooks.fr: Pendant qu'il l'écrivait, sa femme achetait à crédit et devait neuf mois de loyer.
hooks.note: True but NOT in the topic's Wikipedia article — sourcing action required. The novel's article says only that he asked his wife to manage the finances. The detail traces to García Márquez's own recollection: 'the owner of the apartment would wait for us for nine months to pay the rent', with Mercedes obtaining credit from the butcher and baker over the eighteen months of writing. So this card's src must point to a biography source, not to en.wikipedia.org — if the merge script defaults to the Wikipedia slug URL, this one will ship a citation that does not support its claim. The author is never named, so the quiz answer holds.

hooks.en: Her stories were not entertainment. Each unfinished one bought her another morning.
hooks.fr: Chaque conte interrompu à l'aube lui offrait un jour de vie supplémentaire.
hooks.note: Frame story verified: 'Scheherazade begins to tell the king a tale, but does not end it. The king, curious about how the story ends, is thus forced to postpone her execution.' 'Not entertainment' is a rhetorical setup rather than a factual claim — the second sentence carries the checkable content and is accurate. Scheherazade is never named, so the quiz answer holds; 'her' reveals only the narrator's gender, after the reader has already answered.

hooks.en: Nobody is sure what the 'p' in pH actually stands for. Chemists still argue.
hooks.fr: Personne ne sait vraiment ce que signifie le « p » de pH. Le débat dure encore.
hooks.note: Verified verbatim: 'Sørensen did not explain why he used the letter p, and the exact meaning of the letter is still disputed' — candidates include puissance, Potenz, potens, 'potential', or an arbitrary p/q labelling. This is the rare case where a hook is allowed to state uncertainty as the fact. Never touches pH 7. Guillemets used correctly in the fr.

hooks.en: There is a spot in this ocean where the nearest humans are sometimes in orbit.
hooks.fr: Il existe ici un point où les humains les plus proches sont parfois en orbite.
hooks.note: 'Sometimes' is exactly the source's hedge and must stay: 'sometimes the closest human beings are astronauts aboard the International Space Station when it passes overhead' — Point Nemo, 2,688 km from the nearest land. Verified on the Point Nemo article, so cite that page rather than Pacific Ocean. The ocean is never named.

hooks.en: Head for the Pacific through this canal and you come out further east than you went in.
hooks.fr: En traversant vers le Pacifique, on ressort plus à l'est qu'on n'est entré. Comment ?
hooks.note: Worst item in the slice — two independent failures. SPOILER: the quiz is 'links the Pacific Ocean with which other ocean?', answer 'Atlantic Ocean', and both hooks opened by naming the Atlantic — they restate the exact fact just tested, wasting the beat. TRUTH: the Panama Canal article carries no eastward figure at all, and outside sources range from 22.5 to 25 miles (36-40 km) depending on the endpoints measured, so '40 km' states the top of a range as fact. Both rewritten to name only the Pacific, which is in the question rather than the answer, and to drop the number — the direction reversal alone carries the tension. Transit from Colón to Balboa does run southeast, so the claim holds. 87 and 85 chars.

hooks.en: Neither side would sit in the other's city, so the treaty was negotiated in two towns.
hooks.fr: Chaque camp refusait d'aller chez l'autre : la paix a été négociée dans deux villes.
hooks.note: en verified and kept: 'Talks took place in two cities because each side wanted to meet on territory under its own control', Sweden in Protestant-held Osnabrück, France and the Empire in Münster. fr failed on meaning — 'exigeait son propre territoire' reads in French as each side demanding land, a territorial claim, which is not what happened and would have shipped as a factual error in French only. Rewritten to say plainly that neither would go to the other's city. The quiz answer (the sovereign nation-state) is untouched. 84 chars.

hooks.en: The first man ever injected with it was recovering when the supply ran out. He died.
hooks.fr: Le premier homme à en recevoir une injection guérissait. Puis le stock s'est épuisé.
hooks.note: Factual error, corrected. Albert Alexander was not the first patient penicillin treated — Wikipedia is precise: 'the first patient to be treated with injections of penicillin'. Crude penicillin had been applied topically to patients years earlier, so 'the first patient it treated' is false. Everything else checks out: treatment began 12 Feb 1941, 'within 24 hours his temperature had dropped, his appetite had returned and the infection had begun to heal', supply exhausted by the fifth day, 'relapsed and died on 15 March 1941'. Fleming, the quiz answer, is never named — and note the patient's surname was Alexander, which the corrected hook still avoids. 84 and 83 chars.

hooks.en: The fire that destroyed this palace may be the reason its archive survived.
hooks.fr: L'incendie qui a détruit ce palais est peut-être ce qui a sauvé ses archives.
hooks.note: Passes only because of the hedge — do not harden it, and do not let the fact text repeat the popular version. Wikipedia explicitly refutes the widespread 'the fire baked the clay tablets' story: 'the partial burning of Persepolis did not affect the Persepolis Fortification Archive tablets, but may have caused the eventual collapse of the upper part of the northern Fortification wall that preserved the tablets'. So the mechanism is burial by collapsing wall, not baking. 'May be the reason' survives that correction; 'the fire baked them' would not. Achaemenid, the quiz answer, is never named.

hooks.en: The urn carved above the Treasury is scarred with bullet holes. It is solid rock.
hooks.fr: L'urne sculptée au-dessus du Trésor est criblée de balles. Elle est en pierre massive.
hooks.note: Verified verbatim on the Al-Khazneh article: the urn 'in reality is solid sandstone', and 'significant damage from bullets can be seen on the urn, which the Jordanian government attributes to Bedouins who believed the legend' of treasure inside. 'Solid rock' is accurate for sandstone. Jordan, the quiz answer, is never named. 'Criblée de balles' is standard French idiom, not a calque.

hooks.en: The first letter of your alphabet began as a drawing of an ox's head.
hooks.fr: « Alphabet » vient de deux mots phéniciens : le bœuf et la maison.
hooks.note: Verified: the letter 'derives from a Proto-Sinaitic glyph... which depicts an ox's head', named for ʾalp, the West Semitic word for ox, and 'the Phoenician variant gave rise to the Greek alpha, and hence the Latin A'. The fr elides the Greek step (alpha + beta were borrowed from Phoenician ʾalep and bet), which is standard etymological shorthand and acceptable at hook length — but the fact text beneath should spell the Greek step out. Not scored as a spoiler: the answer word 'alphabet' is already in the card title 'Phoenician alphabet', and the hook adds an entirely new fact rather than restating the tested one.

hooks.en: A tree's wood did not come out of the soil. So where did it come from?
hooks.fr: Le bois d'un arbre ne sort pas de la terre. D'où vient-il alors ?

hooks.en: In 1897 an American state legislature came close to voting pi into a different value.
hooks.fr: Jetez des aiguilles sur un parquet, comptez celles qui croisent une rainure : vous obtenez π.
hooks.note: Indiana Pi Bill 1897 confirmed: passed the House 6 Feb without dissent, Senate postponed indefinitely 12 Feb; implied π=3.2. 'Came close' is fair. Does not reveal 3.14. FR uses Buffon's needle (in the Pi article, Monte Carlo section) and is genuinely French-written, not a translation. 85/92 chars.

hooks.en: More than 200 strings inside, and nowhere near that many notes. Where do the extras go?
hooks.fr: Près de vingt tonnes de tension tirent sur le cadre d'un piano à queue. Et il tient.
hooks.note: TWO defects. (1) Spoiler: quiz ans is '88' and the hook opened with 'Eighty-eight keys' — that is the answer verbatim, and the topic name 'Piano' does not otherwise reveal it. (2) Truth: Wikipedia/Piano says tension 'can exceed 20 tons (180 kilonewtons)' — 180 kN is ~18.3 metric tonnes, so French 'plus de vingt tonnes' overstates. 'Près de vingt tonnes' is safe either way. Replacement en keeps the verified >200 strings (~230, 3 per note in treble/tenor) without stating the key count. 86/83 chars.

hooks.en: The famous 'bodies' of Pompeii are plaster, poured into the hollows the bodies left.
hooks.fr: Les corps figés de Pompéi ne sont pas des corps : c'est du plâtre coulé dans un vide.
hooks.note: Fiorelli 1863 technique confirmed: 'devised the technique of injecting plaster into them to recreate the forms of Vesuvius's victims'. Modern casts use resin, but 'the famous bodies' are the plaster ones — accurate. Naming Pompeii is not a spoiler defect: the card title already is Pompeii. Pull is on the weaker side (it half-explains itself) but 'the bodies are not bodies' is a real gap. 84/85 chars.

hooks.en: This city sits inside a municipality that carries a different name. The argument isn't over.
hooks.fr: Soixante-dix mille arbres violets font sa réputation. Aucun n'est originaire d'Afrique.
hooks.note: Confirmed: 'Pretoria is the central part of the City of Tshwane Metropolitan Municipality'; the Tshwane renaming remains a live, unresolved controversy (dedicated 'Proposed change of name' section). FR: 'around 70,000 jacaranda trees' and 'the jacaranda comes from tropical South America' both verbatim — spelled-out 'soixante-dix mille' reads as the estimate it is. Does not reveal the answer 'Three'. 92/87 chars. Minor currency risk on 'the argument isn't over' — recheck at annual review.

hooks.en: Multiplying two big primes is easy. Undoing it is so hard that we hide secrets behind it.
hooks.fr: 3 et 5, 11 et 13 : ces couples de premiers s'arrêtent-ils un jour ? Personne ne l'a prouvé.
hooks.note: RSA framing accurate (hardness is believed, not proved — 'so hard that we hide secrets behind it' correctly describes practice, not a proof claim). FR is the twin prime conjecture: open, unproved. Does not reveal 'itself'. 'Couples de premiers' is elliptical but standard mathematical French and disambiguated by the preceding examples. 89/91 chars.

hooks.en: Europe's press gets the credit. A book printed in Korea with metal type beat it by 78 years.
hooks.fr: Le plus ancien livre imprimé en caractères métalliques est coréen, et date de 1377.
hooks.note: Truth confirmed verbatim on the Jikji article: 'published in Heungdeok Temple in 1377 in 2 volumes, 78 years before Johannes Gutenberg's acclaimed 42-Line Bible'. Defect was spoiler only: the quiz answer is 'Johannes Gutenberg' and the old en named him; the topic name 'Printing press' does not. Replacement withholds the name and makes the reader supply it — stronger pull, and it centres Korea rather than treating Europe as the baseline (rubric §4). FR passes all four and is left unchanged. 91/82 chars.

hooks.en: Chaco's great houses took 200,000 trees. No wheels, no draft animals. How did they arrive?
hooks.fr: Deux cent mille arbres acheminés sans roue ni bête de trait. Comment fait-on ça ?
hooks.note: Truth defect on two counts. Wikipedia: 'The Chacoan structures altogether required the wood of 200,000 coniferous trees, mostly hauled—on foot—from mountain ranges up to 70 miles (110 km) away.' (a) 200,000 is the total for ALL Chacoan structures, not Pueblo Bonito alone — on a Pueblo Bonito card the old wording attributes it to one site. (b) 'over 100 km' inverts 'up to 110 km', which is the maximum, not the norm (Chuska timber came from ~80 km). Corrected en attributes the figure to the great houses collectively and drops the distance. 89/80 chars.

hooks.en: The story that this layout was built to slow typists down may not be true at all.
hooks.fr: Et si ce clavier avait été dessiné pour les télégraphistes, et non pour les dactylos ?
hooks.note: Wikipedia is actually stronger than the hook: 'Contrary to popular belief, the QWERTY layout was not designed to slow the typist down' — the hook understates, which is not a defect. Telegraph thesis present and correctly framed as a competing theory by the conditional 'Et si'. Does not reveal 'typewriter': 'dactylos' is the people, not the machine. 80/85 chars.

hooks.en: She proposed to Albert herself, five days after he arrived. Why was that her job?
hooks.fr: Un homme a tenté de tirer sur elle. Son pistolet était chargé de papier et de tabac.
hooks.note: EN confirmed verbatim: 'the Queen proposed to him on 15 October 1839, just five days after he had arrived at Windsor Castle' — unchanged. FR overstated: Wikipedia says John William Bean (3 July 1842) 'tried to fire a pistol at the Queen, but it was loaded only with paper and tobacco and had too little charge'. 'Lui a tiré dessus' asserts a shot that did not happen — and the whole point of the paper-and-tobacco detail is that it was not a real shot. 'A tenté de tirer' matches the source; the statement still forces the question without asking it. 80/83 chars.

hooks.en: An empire kept its records on knotted string. Nobody can read all of it yet.
hooks.fr: Un empire tenait ses archives sur des cordes nouées. Personne ne sait encore tout lire.

hooks.en: Email wasn't his job. He told a colleague: don't tell anyone we're working on this.
hooks.fr: Le courrier électronique n'était pas sa mission. « N'en parle à personne », dit-il alors.
hooks.note: Confirmed: 'Its development was not directed by his employer, and Tomlinson pursued the idea independently'; the remark 'Don't tell anyone! This isn't what we're supposed to be working on.' The en is reported speech, not in quotation marks, and preserves the sense — acceptable. Does not reveal the decade ('1970s'). FR guillemets used correctly. 82/88 chars.

hooks.en: Violet light scatters even more than blue. So why isn't the sky violet?
hooks.fr: Le violet est encore plus diffusé que le bleu. Pourquoi le ciel n'est-il pas violet ?
hooks.note: FR terminology defect: 'se disperse' is wrong physics in French — dispersion is wavelength separation (prism); scattering is DIFFUSION ('diffusion Rayleigh' is the standard French term, and the topic's own French title). Fixed to 'est encore plus diffusé'. EN is true (Rayleigh ∝ 1/λ⁴) and unchanged. Not scored as a spoiler: the card title is literally the mechanism, and the hook builds past the answer rather than revealing it. 70/84 chars.

hooks.en: Greek manuscripts reached Renaissance Italy in the luggage of refugees. Fleeing what?
hooks.fr: Des livres grecs sont arrivés en Italie dans les bagages de réfugiés. Ils fuyaient quoi ?
hooks.note: Confirmed: 'the fall of Constantinople (1453) generated a wave of émigré Greek scholars bringing precious manuscripts in ancient Greek'. Does not reveal 'Florence'. 'Ils fuyaient quoi ?' is colloquial register rather than 'Que fuyaient-ils ?' — deliberate and punchy, grammatical, keeps the pull; not a defect. 84/88 chars.

hooks.en: This canal was dug so British boats could dodge American guns. That war never came.
hooks.fr: Jusqu'à mille ouvriers y sont morts, surtout du paludisme. Au Canada.
hooks.note: EN confirmed and unchanged: built after 1812 for 'safe passage for military vessels between Montreal and Kingston' avoiding the exposed St Lawrence, and 'no further military engagements have taken place'. FR defect: Wikipedia says 'As many as one thousand of the workers died' — an upper bound (estimates run lower). 'Un millier d'ouvriers y sont morts' states ~1,000 as the figure. 'Jusqu'à mille' matches the source exactly and keeps the 'Au Canada.' punch (malaria cause confirmed). 82/68 chars.

hooks.en: The stream running past these churches is called the Jordan. Someone chose that name.
hooks.fr: Le ruisseau qui coule entre ces églises s'appelle le Jourdain. Ce n'est pas un hasard.
hooks.note: FALSE CLAIM, both languages. 'You can only see that from the air' is not supported and is wrong: Bete Giyorgis sits in a trench 25m x 25m x 30m with 'sheer drops on every side' — visitors stand on the surrounding rock at ground level and look down on the cruciform plan; that is the standard view of the site. Replaced rather than patched, because every truthful patch ('you look down on it', 'its roof is at your feet') restates the quiz answer, 'Carved downward out of solid rock'. New hook uses a verified, non-spoiling fact: 'five churches north of the town's river Jordan, five south of the river', with the New Jerusalem intent explicit in the article. 84/85 chars.

hooks.en: Roman engineers would rather cut a road through a hill than curve around it. Why?
hooks.fr: Le courrier impérial couvrait 80 km par jour sur ces routes. Sans moteur, comment ?
hooks.note: Both claims are verbatim in the topic's own article. EN: 'Roman roads were generally built with the road cutting through the hill, rather than with a serpentine pattern of switchbacks curving around it.' FR: 'On average a relay of horses could carry a letter 80 kilometres (50 mi) in a day.' I initially flagged the 80 km against the Cursus publicus article's 61–100 km/day range, but the Roman roads article states 80 km as the average — sourced and checkable where a reader will look. 80/82 chars.

hooks.en: Most plants don't hunt for water alone. They hire a fungus and pay it in sugar.
hooks.fr: Dans la mangrove, des racines poussent vers le haut, hors de l'eau. Elles respirent.
hooks.note: 'Most plants' verified: mycorrhizas present in '80% of species', ~78% associate with AMF. Exchange verified: 'the plant gives carbohydrates (products of photosynthesis) to the fungus, while the fungus gives the plant water and minerals'. FR pneumatophores accurate. Naming roots in FR is not a spoiler — the card title is Root. 78/83 chars.

hooks.en: Everyone knows what this stone did. Almost nobody knows what it says.
hooks.fr: On sait ce que cette pierre a permis. Pas ce qu'elle raconte.

hooks.en: Rust takes up more room than the iron it replaced. That is how it prises bridges apart.
hooks.fr: À Delhi, un pilier de fer de 1 600 ans résiste encore à la rouille. Pourquoi ?
hooks.note: EN fully confirmed and unchanged: 'the oxides take up more volume than the original metal; this expansion can generate enormous forces', including the 1983 Mianus River Bridge collapse. FR defect: the Delhi pillar DOES rust — 'research published in 2009 showed that corrosion has developed evenly over the surface of the pillar', and the article explicitly debunks the 'absence of corrosion' claim (von Däniken withdrew it). 'Ne rouille toujours pas' ships the myth. 'Résiste encore à la rouille' matches 'high resistance to corrosion' and keeps the pull. Age (erected c. 375–415 CE) supports '1 600 ans'. 86/77 chars.

hooks.en: It isn't three letters. It's one unbroken signal that only looks like S, O and S.
hooks.fr: En 1999, il a cessé d'être le signal de détresse officiel. Par quoi l'a-t-on remplacé ?
hooks.note: Both verbatim: 'transmitted as an unbroken sequence of three dots / three dashes / three dots, with no spaces between the letters'; 'SOS remained the maritime radio distress signal until 1999, when it was replaced by the Global Maritime Distress and Safety System'. Crucially the en does NOT state the dot/dash pattern, so the quiz answer survives. FR takes a different angle from en — exactly what the spec asks for. 80/86 chars.

hooks.en: More than 30,000 rock carvings in the Sahara show river animals — crocodiles among them.
hooks.fr: Plus de 30 000 gravures rupestres du Sahara montrent des animaux de rivière. Des crocodiles.
hooks.note: I expected this one to fail and it does not. Verbatim on the Sahara article: 'Over 30,000 petroglyphs of river animals such as crocodiles survive, with half found in the Tassili n'Ajjer in southeast Algeria.' The number is the article's own, not a rounding. Opens on a statistic, which is the weaker form, but 'crocodiles in the Sahara' is a genuine unclosable gap. FR mirrors the en angle but reads as native French ('gravures rupestres' is the correct term, thin-space thousands). 87/91 chars.

hooks.en: Nothing alive bites harder. Yet a few layers of duct tape hold those jaws shut.
hooks.fr: 590 km en 25 jours, presque sans nager. Ce crocodile a une méthode.
hooks.note: All three claims verbatim: '16,414 N (3,690 lbf)... the strongest bite of any living animal'; 'The jaws of a crocodile can be securely shut with several layers of duct tape' plus 'extremely small and weak muscles to open the jaw'; 'one of them traveled 590 km (370 mi) along the coast in 25 days'. 'Presque sans nager' supported by 'Without having to move around much, sometimes simply by floating, the current-riding behaviour allows for the conservation of energy.' Does not reveal 'largest living reptile'. 78/66 chars.

hooks.en: The famous samurai code was largely written down after the samurai stopped fighting.
hooks.fr: Le fameux code des samouraïs a surtout été écrit une fois les guerres finies.

hooks.en: Nearly 7,000 stone towers still stand on this island. No one agrees what they were for.
hooks.fr: Près de 7 000 tours de pierre se dressent sur cette île. Personne ne sait à quoi elles servaient.
hooks.note: 'Nearly' is the right word and I checked it specifically: 'Today fewer than 7,000 nuraghes remain standing' — 'more than 7,000' would have been the defect. Dispute confirmed: 'There is no consensus on the function of the nuraghes'. Does not reveal 'Italy'. FR is 96 chars — inside the cap but the tightest in the slice; do not lengthen it downstream. 86/96 chars.

hooks.en: A hexagon sits on Saturn's north pole, each side longer than Earth is wide. Why?
hooks.fr: Cette planète est moins dense que l'eau. Assez pour flotter, si la baignoire existait.
hooks.note: Verified: 'The sides of the hexagon are about 14,500 km long... about 2,000 km longer than the diameter of Earth.' The 'Why?' is legitimate — the cause is genuinely unsettled (competing Rossby-wave/barotropic-instability hypotheses), so the gap cannot be closed in the reader's head. FR density 0.687 g/cm³ and the bathtub joke is how the source itself frames it, explicitly flagged as counterfactual. Different angle from en. 79/85 chars.

hooks.en: The cure was proved in a shipboard trial in 1747. The navy acted on it in 1795.
hooks.fr: Au XVIIIe siècle, il tuait plus de marins britanniques que les canons ennemis.
hooks.note: Both dates confirmed: Lind 1747, 'one of the first controlled clinical experiments reported in the history of medicine'; Admiralty daily lemon-juice ration agreed 1795. FR verbatim: 'During the 18th century, scurvy killed more British sailors than wartime enemy action.' Does not name vitamin C, so the quiz answer survives. The 48-year gap is the pull. 78/77 chars.

hooks.en: Some paintings long known as his self-portraits turned out to be his students' work.
hooks.fr: Rembrandt s'est peint à tous les âges. Certains de ces visages ne sont pas de sa main.
hooks.note: Confirmed: 'At one time about ninety paintings were counted as Rembrandt self-portraits, but it is now known that he had his students copy his own self-portraits'; the Rembrandt Research Project 'reduced the autograph count to over forty paintings'. Hedged with 'some', correctly. The word 'self-portraits' contains the quiz answer 'Portrait', but so does the card title — not a hook defect. 83/85 chars.

hooks.en: The tallest living thing on Earth has a name, and an address kept secret.
hooks.fr: Le plus haut être vivant de la Terre a un nom — et une adresse tenue secrète.

hooks.en: He could not read a single language when he invented a way to write one.
hooks.fr: Il ne savait lire aucune langue quand il inventa le moyen d'en écrire une.

hooks.en: Reach a chartered town and dodge capture for a year and a day, and you were free.
hooks.fr: Gagner une ville franche, échapper aux recherches un an et un jour : et l'on était libre.
hooks.note: TRUE, verbatim: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serfdom — 'in England a serf who made his way to a chartered town (i.e. a borough) and evaded recapture for a year and a day obtained his freedom and became a burgher of the town.' No spoiler (quiz answer is 'peasant farmers'). FR FAILED: clause-for-clause mirror of the English, and the impersonal infinitives clash with 'vous étiez libre'. Rewritten with the native impersonal 'et l'on était libre' (89 chars). Note the rule is specifically English — neither line claims otherwise, so it stands.

hooks.en: Why is a second called a 'second'? Something else was cut first.
hooks.fr: Pourquoi une « seconde » porte-t-elle ce nom ? Qu'a-t-on divisé en premier ?
hooks.note: TRUE: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second — 'second' from pars minuta secunda, 'second small part', after the minute (pars minuta prima). No spoiler (answer is 'the Babylonians', never hinted). Strong pull — the gap cannot be closed without the article. FR native, guillemets and espace insécable correct, 76 chars. Ships unchanged.

hooks.en: Chipmakers purify silicon almost perfectly, then deliberately dirty it again. Why?
hooks.fr: On purifie le silicium à l'extrême, puis on le salit exprès. Pourquoi ?
hooks.note: TRUE: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silicon — impurity levels below 1 part in 10^10, then deliberate doping with phosphorus/arsenic/antimony or boron/aluminium/gallium. 'Almost perfectly' is correctly hedged, not overstated. No spoiler (answer is 'sand'). FR idiomatic and independently phrased, 70 chars. Ships unchanged.

hooks.en: Nobody who travelled this road ever called it the Silk Road. The name dates to 1877.
hooks.fr: Aucun voyageur de cette route ne l'a appelée « route de la soie » : le nom date de 1877.
hooks.note: TRUE: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silk_Road — term from German Seidenstraße, 'first popularized in 1877 by Ferdinand von Richthofen'; article confirms Marco Polo never used it and that earlier authors 'never labelled any route a silk one in particular'. No spoiler (answer is 'the Mediterranean and Europe'). FR agreement 'appelée' correct (l' = la route). 87 chars. Ships unchanged.

hooks.en: He wrote a poem about how much this job hurt, and sketched himself buckled under it.
hooks.fr: Il a écrit un poème sur la douleur de ce travail, et s'est dessiné tordu sous le plafond.
hooks.note: TRUE: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sistine_Chapel_ceiling carries the sonnet ('I've grown a goitre by dwelling in this den') and captions the marginal drawing 'Michelangelo's illustration to his poem shows him painting the ceiling'; Barkan compares the posture to Marsyas Bound. Wikipedia hedges with 'may have described', so the hook stays at 'wrote a poem about how much this job hurt' — no overstatement. No spoiler: says 'He', never names Michelangelo. FR is the weakest in the slice (first half tracks the English closely) but is grammatical, correctly spaced and 88 chars — passes.

hooks.en: The same powder that lifts a cake is injected into patients in hospitals. Why?
hooks.fr: La poudre qui fait lever un gâteau s'injecte aussi à l'hôpital. Pourquoi ?
hooks.note: TRUE: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sodium_bicarbonate — 'used in baking as a leavening agent' and 'Intravenous sodium bicarbonate in an aqueous solution is sometimes used for cases of acidosis'. No spoiler (answer is 'carbon dioxide'). FR pronominal passive 's'injecte' is natural, 73 chars. Ships unchanged.

hooks.en: One half of table salt explodes in water. The other was a First World War gas.
hooks.fr: Un des éléments du sel explose dans l'eau ; l'autre servit de gaz de combat en 1915.
hooks.note: TRUE: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sodium states outright 'Sodium spontaneously explodes in the presence of water'; chlorine was released as a weapon at Ypres on 22 April 1915, so the FR's tighter date holds. Not a spoiler: decoding it to 'sodium chloride' requires already knowing the answer. FR uses the correct term 'gaz de combat', espace insécable before ';' present, 83 chars. Ships unchanged.

hooks.en: Twenty-one artists signed a letter against this museum before it opened. Why?
hooks.fr: Vingt et un artistes ont signé une lettre contre ce musée avant son ouverture. Pourquoi ?
hooks.note: TRUE and the count is exact: December 1956 protest letter to director James Johnson Sweeney, 21 named signatories (de Kooning, Motherwell, Gottlieb, Guston, Kline, Avery et al.; Archives of American Art holds the original). Museum opened 1959, so 'before it opened' holds. No spoiler (answer is 'Frank Lloyd Wright'). FR 89 chars, grammatical. Ships unchanged.

hooks.en: It sent a thousand cattle to break the enemy line. They came back the other way.
hooks.fr: Mille bêtes lancées contre la ligne ennemie : le troupeau a fait demi-tour.
hooks.note: FAILED on truth. '40,000 soldiers' is not supported: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Tondibi gives a spread — '20,000 cavalry and 12,900 foot soldiers (Tarikh al-fattash), to 12,500 cavalry and 30,000 infantry, up to 90,000 soldiers in total'. Stating a single precise figure from a disputed range is exactly the defect the spec bans. The cattle detail IS solid and verbatim: 'The Songhai planned to send a stampede of 1,000 cattle to break down the Moroccan lines... repelled by the noise of gunfire and the sound of cannons, which caused the cattle to stampede back towards Songhai lines.' Rebuilt on that: en 80 chars, fr 75. The new version also pulls harder — it withholds the gunfire, so the reader cannot close the gap.

hooks.en: Why does your recorded voice sound wrong to you and normal to everyone else?
hooks.fr: Pourquoi ne reconnaissez-vous pas votre voix enregistrée, alors que tout le monde la reconnaît ?
hooks.note: TRUE: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone_conduction — 'Because the skull conducts lower frequencies better than air, people perceive their own voices to be lower and fuller than others do, and a recording of one's own voice frequently sounds higher than one expects.' No spoiler (answer is 'empty space'). FR FAILED: 'une voix fausse' reads in French first as off-key/out of tune, not 'sounds wrong', and the elliptical second clause strains. Rewritten around the native framing — not recognising your own voice — 96 chars, still inside the cap.

hooks.en: The crack of a whip is not leather hitting anything. So what is it?
hooks.fr: Le claquement d'un fouet n'est pas le cuir qui frappe. Alors, d'où vient-il ?
hooks.note: TRUE: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whip — 'The crack is thus a small sonic boom', the tip exceeding the speed of sound. The hook withholds the answer, so it pulls rather than informs. No spoiler (answer is 'light'). FR 76 chars, idiomatic, espace insécable present. Ships unchanged.

hooks.en: This empire ruled the sea lanes for centuries, then vanished from history until 1918.
hooks.fr: Cet empire régna des siècles sur les mers, puis disparut de l'histoire jusqu'en 1918.

hooks.en: Ten machines entered the contest of 1829. Only one of them finished.
hooks.fr: Dix machines inscrites à l'épreuve de 1829. Une seule est allée au bout.

hooks.en: New land keeps rising out of the sea here. There is no volcano anywhere near.
hooks.fr: Ici, de nouvelles terres sortent de la mer, et aucun volcan dans les parages.
hooks.note: TRUE: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm_archipelago — 'a joint valley landscape that has been shaped – and is still being shaped – by post-glacial rebound' and 'The islands rise by about three millimeters each year.' Sweden has no volcanoes. No number is asserted, so no rounding risk. No spoiler ('here', never names Stockholm). FR 76 chars; 'dans les parages' is native, not translated. Ships unchanged.

hooks.en: Close this strait and the Mediterranean would dry up. It has happened before.
hooks.fr: Fermez ce détroit et la Méditerranée s'assèche. C'est déjà arrivé.
hooks.note: TRUE, and the topic article supports both clauses in one sentence: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strait_of_Gibraltar — 'It is estimated that, were the Strait closed even at today's higher sea level, most water in the Mediterranean basin would evaporate within a thousand years, as it is believed to have done then' (Messinian salinity crisis, c. 5.97 Ma). I checked the obvious objection — the closure then was of the Betic and Rifan corridors, not the modern strait — but the hook's 'it' refers to the drying, which is exactly what Wikipedia affirms. No spoiler (answer is 'Morocco'). FR 65 chars. Ships unchanged.

hooks.en: Fifteen ships sat stuck here for eight years. Their crews staged their own Olympics.
hooks.fr: Quinze navires bloqués ici pendant huit ans. Les équipages ont organisé leurs Jeux olympiques.
hooks.note: TRUE per the topic article's own lead: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Fleet — 'From 1967 to 1975, 15 ships and their crews were trapped in the Suez Canal', and crews 'held the Bitter Lake Olympic Games to complement the 1968 Summer Olympics'. FLAG for the record: many secondary outlets (Mental Floss, Al Jazeera) say fourteen — Wikipedia reconciles this as 14 anchored in the Great Bitter Lake plus SS Observer in Lake Timsah, and the Bitter Lake Association was formed by the fourteen. Fifteen is defensible and sourced, but expect the challenge; if you want zero exposure, 'Fourteen ships sat stuck in one lake for eight years' is fully airtight. No spoiler (answer is 'the Red Sea'). FR 94 chars.

hooks.en: The Sun's outer atmosphere is far hotter than its surface. Nobody knows why.
hooks.fr: L'atmosphère externe du Soleil est bien plus chaude que sa surface. Personne ne sait pourquoi.
hooks.note: EN is TRUE and stays: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coronal_heating_problem — corona 1–3 million K against a ~5,800 K photosphere, and 'Several theories have been proposed to explain this phenomenon, but it is still challenging to determine which is correct', so 'nobody knows why' is not overstated. FAILED on the FR: it dropped 'outer'. The Sun's atmosphere as a whole is NOT hotter than its surface — the chromospheric temperature minimum (~4,100 K) is cooler than the photosphere. Added 'externe' (94 chars). One word, but it is the difference between true and false. No spoiler (answer is 'nuclear fusion').

hooks.en: Sit in a sunny window all day and your skin still makes no vitamin D. Why?
hooks.fr: Une journée entière derrière une vitre ensoleillée : zéro vitamine D. Pourquoi ?
hooks.note: TRUE: ordinary soda-lime window glass absorbs UVB (280–315 nm), the band required for cutaneous vitamin D synthesis, while passing UVA. Minor caveat noted and rejected as immaterial: some low-E glazing transmits marginally more UVB, but no meaningful synthesis occurs behind standard glass. No spoiler (answer is 'the Sun'). FR 80 chars, punchy and independently angled. Ships unchanged.

hooks.en: How did a coastal traders' language become a working language of the African Union?
hooks.fr: Comment la langue de ces marchands est-elle devenue langue de travail de l'Union africaine ?
hooks.note: TRUE: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swahili_language — 'Swahili is also one of the working languages of the African Union and of the Southern African Development Community.' The hook claims only working-language status, not a date, so nothing to overstate. No spoiler (answer is 'Indian Ocean'). Decolonial rubric checked: the arc runs local-to-continental, which elevates rather than diminishes; 'traders' language' is accurate for the Swahili coast context, though remember Kiswahili is the Waswahili's mother tongue, not only a trade lingua franca. FR 92 chars. Ships unchanged.

hooks.en: For four years nobody could build this roof. The answer was hiding in a single sphere.
hooks.fr: Pendant quatre ans, personne ne savait bâtir ce toit. La solution : une seule sphère.
hooks.note: TRUE: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney_Opera_House — design from 1957, 'In mid-1961, the design team found a solution to the problem: the shells all being created as sections from a sphere', each 'sections of a sphere of 75.2 metres radius'. Four years understates the 1957–1963 iteration window rather than overstating it, which is the safe direction. No spoiler (answer is 'Denmark'). FR 85 chars. Ships unchanged.

hooks.en: The composer of this symphony never heard it. He was in the room.
hooks.fr: Le compositeur de cette symphonie ne l'a jamais entendue. Il était pourtant dans la salle.

hooks.en: Two empires spent fifty years fighting over a village with no trees and no food.
hooks.fr: Deux empires se sont battus cinquante ans pour un village sans arbres ni nourriture.
hooks.note: TRUE: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taghaza — Songhai vs Saadi Morocco from c. 1540 (al-Araj's demand) through the 1556–7 and 1586 occupations to the 1590 invasion and Tondibi, i.e. roughly fifty years; and 'all provisions came by caravan: dates from Sijilmasa, camel meat, and millet' with no trees. No spoiler — 'no trees' narrows but never reveals 'slabs of salt'. FR FAILED on grammar: 'se sont disputés' is wrong — with se disputer qqch the reflexive is the indirect object and the direct object follows the verb, so there is no agreement ('se sont disputé'). Word order was also awkward. Rewritten with 'se sont battus... pour' (83 chars), which is both correct and more natural.

hooks.en: History books called them extinct. Six in ten Puerto Ricans carry their DNA today.
hooks.fr: Les livres les disaient éteints. Six Portoricains sur dix portent encore leur ADN.
hooks.note: TRUE on both clauses: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taíno — 'Histories of the Caribbean traditionally describe the Taíno as extinct' and '61% of Puerto Ricans' carry mitochondrial DNA of Indigenous origin. 'Six in ten' rounds 61% DOWN, so it does not breach the no-rounding-up rule. Precision note for the record: the 61% figure is mitochondrial (maternal-line) DNA; autosomal studies put some Indigenous ancestry higher still, so the hook understates if anything. Spoiler judged FALSE — it never states the answer; but flagging that 'Puerto Ricans' transitively implies 'the Caribbean', so this card must stay strictly post-answer. Strongest decolonial hook in the slice. FR 82 chars. Ships unchanged.

hooks.en: Eight thousand soldiers guard a tomb nobody has opened in fifty years of digging.
hooks.fr: Huit mille soldats gardent un tombeau toujours pas ouvert, cinquante ans après.

hooks.en: A thousand years ago, this book already listed seven rules for testing a drug.
hooks.fr: Il y a mille ans, ce livre énonçait déjà sept règles pour tester un médicament.
hooks.note: TRUE and the count is exact: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Canon_of_Medicine — 'The Canon contains seven rules for experimenting with new drugs, taken partly from Galen.' Completed c. 1025, so 'a thousand years ago' is accurate to the year in 2026. The hook claims listing, not inventing, so the Galen provenance creates no overstatement. No spoiler (answer is 'Ibn Sina'). FR 78 chars. Ships unchanged.

hooks.en: The blue this print is famous for was a chemical newly shipped in from Europe.
hooks.fr: Le bleu qui a rendu cette estampe célèbre était un pigment chimique importé d'Europe.
hooks.note: TRUE: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Great_Wave_off_Kanagawa — Prussian blue (bero ai) 'was imported from Holland beginning in 1820... after its arrival in Japan in large quantities in 1829', print made late 1831. I specifically checked the via-China objection; the article says Holland, so 'from Europe' is right and 'newly' is right (two years before the print). No spoiler (answer is 'Hokusai'). Pull is the softest of the passes but real: a Japanese icon depending on a just-landed European chemical. FR 85 chars. Ships unchanged.

hooks.en: A pencil note on this painting calls the painter a madman. The handwriting is his.
hooks.fr: Une note au crayon sur ce tableau traite le peintre de fou. L'écriture est la sienne.
hooks.note: FAILED on truth: it is not a canvas. The 1893 National Museum version that carries the inscription is oil, tempera and pastel on CARDBOARD (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Scream). 'Toile' in the FR had the same defect. Everything else checks out: the pencil line reads 'Kan kun være malet af en gal Mand!' ('could only have been painted by a madman!'), long assumed to be a critic's, and infrared analysis established 'the comment was added by Munch'. Swapped canvas/toile for painting/tableau — 'tableau' is support-neutral in French, so it fixes both. No spoiler: says 'the painter', never names Munch. en 81, fr 84. Version nuance for the record: only the 1893 version bears the note.

hooks.en: The painter called this canvas a failure in a letter to a friend.
hooks.fr: Le peintre a qualifié cette toile d'échec dans une lettre à un ami.
hooks.note: TRUE: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Starry_Night — Van Gogh 'referred to the painting as a failure' writing to Émile Bernard, late November 1889. 'A friend' is correct and not 'his brother' — I checked the recipient specifically, since Theo would have made the line false. Also confirmed 'oil-on-canvas', so 'this canvas'/'cette toile' is literally accurate here (unlike The Scream). No spoiler (answer is 'Vincent van Gogh'). en 64, fr 66. Ships unchanged.

hooks.en: A thousand years on, nobody knows the real name of the woman who wrote it.
hooks.fr: De l'autrice, il ne reste qu'un surnom de cour : son vrai nom est perdu.
hooks.note: Fact confirmed on Murasaki Shikibu ('her personal name is unknown'; Shikibu = her father's ministry, Murasaki a court sobriquet) — note it lives on the author's article, not the Genji article. Quiz ans 'Japan' not revealed. FR only fault: regular space before the colon; NBSP inserted.

hooks.en: His handwritten manuscript sat forgotten under dust in a London typing office for months.
hooks.fr: Il est devenu écrivain après un roman anglais qui montrait les Nigérians en bouffons.
hooks.note: EN confirmed verbatim: 'the agency retrieved the manuscripts already covered with dust from a corner of the office' after months of silence; handwritten confirmed. FR confirmed on Chinua Achebe: 'He decided to become a writer after reading Mister Johnson by Joyce Cary because of the book's portrayal of its Nigerian characters as either savages or buffoons.' Achebe not named in either. Ships unchanged.

hooks.en: Some nations plant a fourth sister beside the three. What is she there for?
hooks.fr: Une quatrième sœur existe : le tournesol, planté à la bordure nord du jardin. Pourquoi là ?
hooks.note: FR confirmed verbatim: 'several Native American groups also planted sunflowers on the north edges of their gardens as a fourth sister'. (A second fourth sister, Rocky Mountain beeplant, exists among the Tewa — EN's 'some nations' correctly covers both.) Quiz ans 'Beans' not revealed. FR fault: spacing before ':' and '?' only.

hooks.en: Twice a day the current in London's river stops, turns round and runs inland.
hooks.fr: Au cœur de Londres, le fleuve peut monter et descendre de sept mètres. Deux fois par jour.
hooks.note: EN true and pulls (tide reversal to Teddington; 'rises and falls twice a day'). FR FAILED pull: it names 'la marée' and then explains the effect in the same breath — informs instead of opening a gap. Rewrote FR onto the 7 m range (WP: 'up to 7 m', so 'peut monter') without naming the cause. Quiz ans 'Thames' still not named.

hooks.en: Its oldest inscriptions usually run upwards — from the bottom of the line to the top.
hooks.fr: Ses plus vieilles inscriptions se lisent souvent vers le haut. Pourquoi écrire en montant ?
hooks.note: OVERSTATED ATTRIBUTION. Wikipedia says bottom-to-top of the ancestral Libyco-Berber script and hedges: 'The writing was usually from the bottom to the top, although right-to-left, and even other orders, were also found.' 'Traditionally it was written upwards' presents a usual tendency of an older script as a settled rule of Tifinagh. Rewrote both to 'oldest inscriptions' + 'usually/souvent'. New FR also removes the self-answer in the old one.

hooks.en: Most cats avoid deep water. This one crosses rivers eight kilometres wide.
hooks.fr: Deux taches blanches derrière les oreilles. Il s'en sert pour parler.
hooks.note: EN confirmed verbatim: 'easily transverses rivers as wide as 8 km'. FR confirmed: 'Tigers will move their ears around to display the white spots, particularly during aggressive encounters and between mothers and cubs' — so 'pour parler' is the article's own communication reading, not the disputed eyespot-mimicry hypothesis. No punctuation needing NBSP. Ships unchanged.

hooks.en: In 2016 the court at The Hague jailed a man for destroying buildings here. A first.
hooks.fr: En 2016, La Haye a condamné un homme pour avoir détruit des bâtiments ici. Une première.
hooks.note: HELD AND REPLACED, two independent failures. (1) SPOILER: quiz ans is 'Learning and books'; a hook about a librarian and 350,000 manuscripts hands that back. (2) 'metal trunks' is not in either Wikipedia article — it comes from press/Hammer's book, so it fails the src rule. Replaced with the ICC conviction (confirmed: al-Mahdi, 2016, nine mausoleums + Sidi Yahya Mosque, 'the first time the ICC had indicted an individual for the war crime of attacking religious buildings or historical monuments'). Decolonial check: names no ethnicity, no 'discovered', centres the loss to Timbuktu.

hooks.en: France ran on Greenwich time until the war. It has never gone back.
hooks.fr: Un des fuseaux horaires français ne compte pas un seul habitant. Lequel ?
hooks.note: EN confirmed: 'In 1911, Metropolitan France adopted GMT+0 as its official time, and used it until 1940' and 'GMT+1 has since then remained the official time'. FR confirmed by cross-check: Clipperton Island is UTC-8 and Wikipedia calls it 'uninhabited', population 0. EN names France but so does the card title, so no incremental spoiler. FR fault: spacing before '?' only.

hooks.en: Until 2018 a train leaving Vladivostok departed on Moscow's clock, seven hours away.
hooks.fr: En 2010, la Russie a supprimé deux fuseaux horaires. Elle les a rétablis quatre ans plus tard.
hooks.note: EN confirmed: 'Until 2018, all timetables on Russian Railways (except Sakhalin railways) followed Moscow Time' — Vladivostok UTC+10 vs Moscow UTC+3 = seven hours. FR confirmed: 28 March 2010 'led to abolition of two of the eleven time zones'; restored 26 October 2014, i.e. four years. No punctuation needing NBSP. Ships unchanged.

hooks.en: Tokyo stopped being a city in 1943. It has been something else ever since.
hooks.fr: Tokyo administre une île perdue à 1 850 km dans le Pacifique. Comment est-ce possible ?
hooks.note: EN confirmed verbatim: 'In 1943, Tokyo City merged with Tokyo Prefecture to form the Tokyo Metropolis'. FR FAILED: it was a word-for-word rendering of the EN, which the spec forbids — a French reader gets the identical angle. Rewrote onto Minami Torishima, confirmed as 'at 1,850 km the most distant island from central Tokyo'. Quiz ans 'Kyoto' untouched in both.

hooks.en: If enamel is see-through, where does the colour of your teeth come from?
hooks.fr: Pourquoi le corps détruit-il les cellules qui fabriquent l'émail avant même que la dent perce ?
hooks.note: EN supported: enamel is translucent and 'the yellow color of the dentin is visible' through it — 'see-through' is colloquial for translucent and the substantive claim (colour comes from underneath) is exact. FR confirmed verbatim and precisely: 'At some point before the tooth erupts into the mouth, but after the maturation stage, the ameloblasts are broken down.' FR fault: spacing before '?' only.

hooks.en: Which country records the most tornadoes for its size? Not the United States.
hooks.fr: L'échelle qui classe les tornades ne mesure pas le vent : elle mesure les dégâts.
hooks.note: EN holds: Wikipedia says 'Of all countries, the United Kingdom has the highest incidence of tornadoes per unit area of land' — so 'Not the United States' is correct. Note the hook wisely does not name the winner, which also insulates it against the UK/Netherlands source split. FR confirmed: the Fujita/EF scales 'rate tornadoes by damage caused'. FR fault: spacing before ':' only.

hooks.en: In Turing's first version of the game there is no machine: you must tell a man from a woman.
hooks.fr: Turing avait fixé une échéance : l'an 2000. Et un seuil : tromper le juge trois fois sur dix.
hooks.note: EN confirmed: 'Player A is a man, player B is a woman and player C (who plays the role of the interrogator) is of either sex' — no machine in the first statement. FR confirmed: 'in about fifty years' time... an average interrogator will not have more than 70% chance of making the right identification', i.e. fooled 3 times in 10, and Turing's own 'at the end of the century' supports l'an 2000. FR fault: spacing before both colons.

hooks.en: The best-known pharaoh in the world was erased from Egypt's own king lists.
hooks.fr: Le pharaon le plus connu au monde avait été effacé des listes royales égyptiennes.

hooks.en: He ruled Samarkand and mapped 994 stars without a telescope. His own son had him killed.
hooks.fr: Un sextant de 40 mètres, en partie creusé dans le sol. Pourquoi enterrer un instrument ?
hooks.note: TWO ROUNDING/OVERSTATEMENT DEFECTS. (1) EN: the Zij-i-Sultani catalogued 994 stars, not 'a thousand' — rounding up stated as fact. Used the exact figure and added 'without a telescope', which is both true and a stronger pull. Assassination by his son Abd al-Latif in 1449 confirmed. (2) FR: 'dormait sous terre' overstates — Wikipedia says only 'part of the sextant' was built underground, 'in a ditch roughly 2 meters wide'. Radius 40.04 m confirmed. Rewrote FR to 'en partie creusé dans le sol' and turned it into a question. Quiz ans 'Timur' not revealed.

hooks.en: Why does a brand-new one-terabyte drive show up as only 931 gigabytes?
hooks.fr: Il existe une unité officielle, le kibioctet, que presque personne n'utilise. Pourquoi ?
hooks.note: EN arithmetic exact: 1 TB = 10^12 bytes / 2^30 = 931.32 GiB, which is what a drive reports. FR: kibioctet is the correct French IEC 80000-13 term and low adoption is a soft, defensible claim. Marginal note, not a fail: the hook implies TB > GB and the quiz ans is 'Terabyte' — but the reader has already answered and no option list is restated. FR fault: spacing before '?' only.

hooks.en: Why does Morocco's oldest university carry the name of a city in Tunisia?
hooks.fr: En 1396, Ibn Khaldoun a offert son propre manuscrit à sa bibliothèque. Que garde-t-elle encore ?
hooks.note: EN confirmed: 'The Arabic name of the university means University of the People from Kairouan', the al-Fihri family having migrated from Kairouan, Tunisia. FR confirmed verbatim: 'the original copy of Ibn Khaldun's book Al-'Ibar (including the Muqaddimah) gifted by the author in 1396'. Quiz ans 'Fatima al-Fihri' not revealed by either. FR fixes: spacing before '?', and 'confié' (entrusted/lent) tightened to 'offert' to match 'gifted'.

hooks.en: A whole country fits inside one city, and still found room for a railway.
hooks.fr: Un pays entier tient dans une seule ville, et il y a pourtant une gare.

hooks.en: For part of the year, swimmers sit in a rock pool right on the lip of the drop.
hooks.fr: Certaines nuits de pleine lune, un arc-en-ciel se forme ici. Sans le moindre soleil.
hooks.note: EN confirmed: the Devil's Pool, 'an infinity pool that sits on the lip of Victoria Falls', swimmable 'usually between September and December' — 'for part of the year' is correctly hedged. FR confirmed: 'At full moon, a moonbow can also be seen.' 'Sans le moindre soleil' reads as no sun in the sky, which is true; I considered and rejected the pedantic objection that moonlight is reflected sunlight. Quiz ans 'Zambezi' not named. No punctuation needing NBSP. Ships unchanged.

hooks.en: Without pine resin rubbed on the hair, a bow slides over the string and barely sounds.
hooks.fr: Pendant des siècles, les cordes du violon ne sortaient pas d'un atelier mais d'un abattoir.
hooks.note: EN FACTUAL DEFECT: rosin is not 'a sticky powder'. Wikipedia describes 'cakes or blocks of rosin' that players 'rub on their bow hair', obtained 'from pine trees and other plants, mostly conifers'. Corrected to 'pine resin' and softened the effect to 'slides over the string and barely sounds', matching the article's 'grip the strings and make them speak'. FR passes untouched and is verified (historic gut strings from animal intestine); quiz ans 'Four' not revealed.

hooks.en: Why does the Washington Monument change colour 150 feet up?
hooks.fr: En 1854, une pierre offerte par le pape a été détruite ici, en pleine nuit. Par qui ?
hooks.note: EN ROUNDED AND UNDERCOUNTED. The change is at the 150 ft level of a 555 ft shaft = 27%, sold as 'the bottom quarter'; and Wikipedia says 'The three different shades of marble can be distinguished', not two. Replaced with the exact height, which is also a sharper hook. FR confirmed verbatim: the Pope's Stone from Pius IX 'was destroyed by members of the anti-Catholic, nativist American Party, better known as the Know-Nothings, during the early morning hours of March 6, 1854' — 'Par qui ?' correctly withholds it. Quiz ans 'Aluminium' absent from both. FR fault: spacing before '?'.

hooks.en: Why did New Zealand let commissioners from Australia choose the site of its capital?
hooks.fr: Une partie du centre-ville repose sur un fond de port qu'un séisme a soulevé en 1855.
hooks.note: EN confirmed: Australian commissioners, chosen for neutrality, declared the city suitable 'because of its central location in New Zealand and its good harbour' when the capital moved in 1865. FR confirmed: the 1855 quake 'caused vertical movements of two to three metres... raising land out of the harbour... Much of this land was subsequently reclaimed and is now part of the central business district.' Quiz ans 'Wellington' not named in either. No punctuation needing NBSP. Ships unchanged.

hooks.en: Some of them fight by bursting open and throwing their own DNA over the invader.
hooks.fr: Le pus n'est pas de la saleté. Ce sont vos propres cellules, tombées au combat.
hooks.note: EN confirmed and correctly hedged with 'some of them': suicidal NETosis is 'followed by the rupture of the plasma membrane', releasing DNA nets — vital NETosis spares the cell, which is why 'some' matters. FR FAILED pull: it states the fact and explains it in the same sentence (diapedesis), so nothing is left open. Rewrote onto pus, confirmed as 'dead leukocytes... mostly neutrophils'. Quiz ans 'White blood cells' still not named.

hooks.en: The first country where women could vote still would not let them stand.
hooks.fr: Premier pays où les femmes ont voté. Pas le premier où elles pouvaient être élues.

hooks.en: The navy funded the robot that found the wreck. First it had to map two nuclear submarines.
hooks.fr: L'épave est rongée par une bactérie qui porte le nom du navire. Combien de temps lui reste-t-il ?
hooks.note: BOTH SIDES FAILED. FR is the serious one: the '180 kg de fer par jour' figure appears nowhere on Halomonas titanicae or the wreck article — unsourced, and it also credits one species for what the article calls rusticles, 'bioconcretious structures formed by a consortium of microorganisms'. Dropped the number entirely. EN was loose on causation: Argo was Navy-sponsored deep-search hardware, and 'In 1984 the Navy sent Ballard and Argo to map the wrecks of the sunken nuclear submarines USS Thresher and USS Scorpion' was the assignment, not the build spec. Reworded to sequence rather than purpose. Quiz ans 'Titanic' still unnamed.

hooks.en: The first powered aeroplane was paid for, and built, by a bicycle shop.
hooks.fr: Le premier avion motorisé a été payé et construit par un magasin de vélos.

hooks.en: The empire is long gone. Russian still calls a coachman by the word it left behind.
hooks.fr: Le mot russe qui désigne le cocher vient d'un empire disparu depuis six siècles.
hooks.note: SPOILER in EN: quiz ans is 'Mongol Empire' and the hook says 'its Mongol word' — the card title 'Yam (route)' does not otherwise contain it, so this is an incremental give-away. Rewrote EN to withhold the empire, which strengthens the pull. Etymology itself confirmed: 'The word yam was adopted by the Russians' and 'The coachman performing the yam service was called a yamshchik'. FR was already clean and names no empire; kept unchanged.

hooks.en: This dynasty's astronomers fixed the year at 365.2425 days. Europe got there 300 years later.
hooks.fr: Un empereur de cette dynastie a supprimé les pièces : on ne payait plus qu'en papier.
hooks.note: SPOILER in EN: quiz ans is 'Kublai Khan' and the hook opens 'Kublai's astronomers'. Swapped to 'This dynasty's astronomers'. Fact itself confirmed on Guo Shoujing: 'In 1280, Guo completed the calendar, calculating a year to be 365.2425 days' — the Gregorian reform reached the same mean year in 1582, so '300 years later' is right to within two years. FR confirmed: 'under Külüg Khan coins were completely replaced by paper money', and it correctly says 'un empereur' rather than naming Kublai. FR fault: spacing before ':'.

hooks.en: There is a tomb for him in Nanjing. There is no body in it.
hooks.fr: Le chef des flottes impériales chinoises était un eunuque musulman, capturé enfant.
hooks.note: EN asserts a DISPUTED claim.
